ActivityEmbedding.description: One embedding declared on a class of the graph.

class.description: The class IRI the embedding covers.

oneOf.description: The newest commit the serving version covers.

The newest failure of the embed job when it is newer than the
embedding's last update and the embedding is not ready and current.

lag_commits.description: Commits the serving version is behind `published_seq`.

oneOf.description:
While `backfilling`: the instances the pass visited, and the class's
instance count when one bounded read gives it.

ActivityError.description:
A tenant-safe failure: a stable code and a short message. Unknown
failures carry `job_failed`; the item id identifies the job for an
operator.

retryable.description: True when a retry can succeed without a change by the user.

oneOf.description:
The failure of a failed item, or the last failure of an item that
waits for or runs a retry (`retryable: true`).

finished_at_micros.description: Set for succeeded, failed and cancelled items.

stage.description:
Machine stage, for example `compacting_truth`, `building`,
`publishing`, `rdf_partitions_pending`, `admission_deferred`, or the
import stage.

subject.description:
What the job works on beyond the graph: the export id, or the graph a
fork writes.

oneOf.description: The commit the job works toward, when it has one.

ActivityProgress.description: How far a job has come. `total` is absent when the job does not know it.

ActivityWriteLimit.description:
The unpublished commits on the graph head against the write path's limits
on them. Past any `soft_*` limit each write waits a little (the wait grows
toward the hard limit); at any `max_*` (hard) limit a write is refused with
a retryable `429 ingest_busy` until the index catches up.

pending_bytes.description:
What the unpublished commits store for strong reads: their runs'
bytes, or the decoded text of a commit without runs.

pending_records.description: Statements the unpublished commits assert or retract.

soft_pending_commits.description: Where writes start to slow down. 0 when the server has no soft limit.

AddEntityTypeOp.description:
Declare a new entity type. Idempotent: a no-op if the name already exists.
Pair with `widen_relation` (in the same request, ordered before it) to add
a brand-new type to an existing relation's domain or range.

name.description: Display name of the new entity type.

AddPropertyOp.description:
Declare a new typed scalar property field (e.g. `status`, `dueDate`,
`budget`) so a commit's `entity_properties` can write it on a live graph.
Additive: every existing record stays valid and no migration is needed.
Unlike `define_ontology` (which recreates the graph ontology), this bumps
the ontology version and registers just the field. Idempotent — a no-op
if a field with this name already exists (the existing type is kept).

allowed_values.description:
Optional **enforced** allowed-value set (a SHACL `sh:in`): a commit
whose value for this field is outside the set is rejected at write
time, so a controlled vocabulary is a one-line declaration instead of
a separate shapes graph. Only for enumerable types
(`keyword`/`text`/`i64`/`bool`); rejected on `f64`/`date_time`/`bytes`.
Use `set_property_constraint` to tighten an existing field.

name.description:
Display name of the new property field (case-insensitive; a commit's
`entity_properties[].field` resolves to it).

required.description: Advisory required flag recorded on the field (not enforced on commit).

value_type.description:
`bool` | `i64` | `f64` | `date_time` | `keyword` | `text` (default) |
`bytes`. The commit path rejects values whose type doesn't match.

AddRelationOp.description:
Declare a new relation type (e.g. `HAS_PHASE`, `ASSIGNED_TO`) with its own
domain and range, by name. The named domain/range entity types must
already exist (add them earlier in the same request with `add_entity_type`
if new). Idempotent: a no-op if a relation with this name already exists —
use `widen_relation` to grow an existing relation's domain/range. Optional
fields default exactly as the ontology spec importer does.

domain.description: Entity-type names allowed as the source (domain).

name.description: Display name of the new relation.

range.description: Entity-type names allowed as the target (range).

symmetric.description: Whether the relation is symmetric (default false).

transitive.description: Whether the relation is transitive (default false).

AddSuperTypesOp.description:
Add direct parent classes to an existing entity type. All named classes
must already exist, or be declared earlier in the same request with
`add_entity_type`. Existing links are skipped, so the op is idempotent.
Removing a parent is not additive and requires an explicit migration.

entity_type.description: Entity type whose direct parents should grow.

super_types.description: Direct parent entity-type names to add.

AdditiveOntologyEvolveOp.description: Governed proposal operation restricted to additive ontology changes.

AdditiveOntologyEvolveRequest.description: Additive-only ontology proposal helper for structured-output systems.

AnalyticBinding.description: One solution: each query variable bound to a resolved entity.

AnalyticCombinator.description:
A group-graph-pattern combinator folded over an analytic query's base BGP —
the SPARQL operators beyond a plain conjunctive join. Each carries its own
basic graph pattern (the right side); combinators apply left-to-right in the
order given. Externally tagged (`{"union": [ … ]}`, `{"optional": [ … ]}`, …).

oneOf.description: `{ base } UNION { patterns }` — multiset union of the two solution sets.

union.description: `{ base } UNION { patterns }` — multiset union of the two solution sets.

oneOf.description:
`base OPTIONAL { patterns }` — left join; unmatched base rows are kept with
the optional variables unbound.

optional.description:
`base OPTIONAL { patterns }` — left join; unmatched base rows are kept with
the optional variables unbound.

oneOf.description:
`base MINUS { patterns }` — drop base rows compatible with a right solution
they share a variable with.

minus.description:
`base MINUS { patterns }` — drop base rows compatible with a right solution
they share a variable with.

oneOf.description:
`base FILTER EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with a compatible right
solution (a semijoin).

exists.description:
`base FILTER EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with a compatible right
solution (a semijoin).

oneOf.description:
`base FILTER NOT EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with no compatible
right solution.

not_exists.description:
`base FILTER NOT EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with no compatible
right solution.

AnalyticQueryRequest.description:
A basic-graph-pattern query: a conjunction of triple patterns evaluated over
the graph's current edges (joined on shared variables), served from the
conformant published RDF dataset.

combinators.description:
Group-graph-pattern combinators (UNION / OPTIONAL / MINUS / EXISTS /
NOT EXISTS) folded over the base `patterns`, left-to-right. Empty (the
default) leaves the query a plain conjunctive BGP.

oneOf.description:
Read consistency (A3 serving; A5 default). `eventual` (the **default**)
serves ENTIRELY from the last published segment RDF family (the
maintenance-owned, asserted-only default) at its watermark — no in-memory
gap fold, so the query stays available while background indexing lags — and
surfaces the served watermark on `snapshot.served_at_seq`. Eventual serving
requires a published dataset; a graph with none yet returns a retryable 429.
`strong` (explicit opt-in) succeeds only when the immutable published
generation itself covers head. Otherwise it returns retryable
`strong_read_pending`; no query folds mutable WAL state.

limit.description: Cap the number of returned bindings.

max_fetched_bytes.description:
Companion byte ceiling on block bytes fetched by the query. Clamped to the
server's `MAX_ANALYTIC_FETCHED_BYTES`; also trips `truncated_by_read_budget`.

max_object_reads.description:
Fail-closed ceiling on object reads (GETs) the query's scans may issue —
the per-request object-storage cost cap. Clamped to the server's
`MAX_ANALYTIC_OBJECT_READS`; when hit, the scan stops and the response's
`truncated_by_read_budget` flag is set.

max_solutions.description:
Fail-closed ceiling on the intermediate join solution set. Clamped to the
server's `MAX_ANALYTIC_SOLUTIONS`; when the join hits it the result is
partial and the response's `truncated` flag is set. Distinct from `limit`,
which is a caller-requested cap on the final, complete result.

oneOf.description:
A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `eventual`, a floor not yet covered by the
published dataset returns a retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429 (poll
until it lands); under `strong` the floor is satisfied by construction and a
floor above head is a client error. `None` == no floor.

truncated.description:
True when a safety cap (the intermediate-solution ceiling) cut the join —
the solution set is partial. Not set by `limit`, which is caller-requested.

truncated_by_read_budget.description:
True when the per-request object-read budget (`max_object_reads` /
`max_fetched_bytes`) was hit, so scans stopped early — the result may be
incomplete.

AnalyticTerm.description:
A triple-pattern term: a named query variable (`{"var": "x"}`) or a fixed
entity (`{"entity": {...}}`).

AnalyticTriplePattern.description:
One triple pattern of an analytic (BGP) query. The predicate is a relation
name, resolved server-side. In an inference rule body the predicate may also
be the reserved [`RDF_TYPE_PREDICATE`] for a type-membership constraint.

AskStructuredQuery.description:
The constrained structured plan: the entity type the answer set is
restricted to (the QALD-class-task shape), plus — when the question admits
them — a relation and an anchor entity. Every slot is real vocabulary by
construction (decoded under the shortlist trie or forced by a type
signature, and server-verified ⊆ the shortlist either way).

target_type.description:
Decoded target entity type (a declared class, subtype-inclusive at
execution).

CalibrationServingDefaults.description:
Calibration serving default derived from a promoted `calibration` run:
the Platt scaler the retrieval-premise producer applies when a request
supplies no inline `calibration`. The scaler is fit on the BM25 entity
channel (the same channel query-driven premise requests use) from
execution-verified outcomes.

model_id.description: The retrieval channel the scaler was fitted on.

run.description: The promoted registry run this scaler came from.

snapshot_commit_seq.description:
The snapshot the scaler was fitted at (its split pin — provenance;
the producer re-pins the manifest to the served snapshot).

CapturedSignal.description:
One captured signal as the range reader returns it: the stored envelope
plus the commit seq of the object it was flushed at (the temporal-split
coordinate trainers filter on).

last_commit_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the head commit.

oneOf.description:
Write-time validation outcome (roadmap item 9 M0). Present only when the
commit raised at least one warning; absent on a fully-conformant commit.
M0 reports structural domain/range mismatches in `warn` mode (never
blocks); `reject` mode and SHACL shapes arrive with the constraints work.

drain_pressure.description:
R27d(1) advisory pacing telemetry: the WAL drain pressure at ack time as a
`0.0`–`1.0` tail-fill ratio. Present only once the tail is over half full.
Clients SHOULD reduce write concurrency as this rises; advisory only.

oneOf.description:
Active graph-schema SHACL validation outcome. Present only when the graph
has an activated schema shape set and the commit violated or warned on it.

throttle_ms.description:
R27d(1) advisory pacing telemetry: the pacing latency this write ack
absorbed — head-lane serialization plus admission wait — in whole
milliseconds. Present only past a noise floor (a fast commit omits it) and
mirrored to the `X-LBB-Throttle-Ms` response header. Clients SHOULD reduce
write concurrency as this rises; it is never load-bearing for correctness.

written_properties.description:
Property fields actually written by this commit, per entity (canonical
field names, resolved against the ontology). Lets a writer confirm a
property landed without a follow-up read. Present only on a fresh commit
that carried `entity_properties`; empty on idempotent replays and no-ops.

ConformanceReport.description:
Closed-world validation report for a commit. Mirrors the shape of a SHACL
`sh:ValidationReport`: `conforms` plus one `results` entry per violation.

focus_node.description: The focus node the constraint was evaluated on (the entity name/id).

value.description: The offending value (the endpoint's entity-type name).

DateBucketGranularity.description:
The calendar unit a [`SparqlGroupKey::DateBucket`] truncates a datetime to.
Truncation is in UTC; the label is the bucket's start as a sortable string.

DecorationStatus.description:
One row of the engine's decoration-status catalog: whether a declarable
ontology decoration is actually acted on by the engine (`enforced`), recorded
and meaningful but not the mechanism (`advisory`), or present-but-unwired
(`reserved`). The catalog is engine-global — identical for every graph — so
the API, MCP, and console agree on what the engine *acts on* versus what it
merely *remembers*. See `decoration_catalog`.

effect.description: One line: what the engine does with it (or that it does nothing yet).

Embedding.description:
The persisted embedding (`…/embeddings/epoch=<e>/<name>/embedding.json`):
the latest declaration and which version serves, builds, and was served
before.

previous.description: The version that served before the last switch (one rollback).

EmbeddingBackfill.description:
A pass over every instance of the class: the first backfill of a
version, or a rescan when the commit deltas are not available.

cursor.description: The last instance IRI done; the next page starts after it.

rescan.description: A rescan of a ready version (the delta chain was not available).

target_seq.description: The published commit the pass reads.

EmbeddingCandidate.description:
One fact the instances of a class could give their text, measured on a
sample of the class.

chosen.description: The field is in the previewed recipe.

coverage.description: Share of the sampled instances with at least one value (0 to 1).

examples.description: Up to three values from the sample, as they appear in the text.

max.description: Values per instance the field keeps (the recipe's `max`).

name.description: The line name the field gets in the text.

path.description:
The path as a recipe stores it: one predicate IRI, or a link and the
predicate read on the linked entity.

EmbeddingCandidateKind.description: What kind of value a candidate field gives the text.

dim.description: The vector dimension; the model's when absent.

exclude.description: Names or IRIs to drop from the automatic choice.

from.description:
The fields in text order. Absent: the server picks them from a sample
of the class (the label, frequent text literals, the labels of linked
entities) and stores the result.

model.description: The model id; the catalog's embedding model when absent.

name.description: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}`; defaults to the class's local name.

title.description:
The field that names each hit, as a path (`display_name`,
`schema:name`, `<https://…>`, `company/label`). Absent on a new
embedding: the ontology's name property (see
[`EmbeddingTitleSource`]); absent on an existing one: its name stays.

EmbeddingField.description:
A resolved field: the predicate IRIs of the path (one or two), the name
in the text, and the value cap.

name.description:
The word before the colon in the text; defaults to the local name of
the first predicate.

EmbeddingFieldSpec.description:
A field as a caller writes it: a path, or a path with a display name and
a value cap.

oneOf.description: `label`, `description`, `calls/label`, `rdfs:label`, `<https://…>`.

model_id.description:
The embedding model of the graph: every serving embedding of the
graph uses it, so one query vector serves a search over all classes.
Absent before the first declaration (the catalog's model applies then).

next_model_id.description:
The model a move goes to: every embedding builds a version with it,
and the graph switches when all are ready (the search keeps
`model_id` until then).

EmbeddingManifest.description:
One version (`…/<name>/v<n>/manifest.json`, CAS): its recipe, its runs,
and how far it covers the graph.

oneOf.description: The published commit the version has embedded through.

runs.description: Oldest first. A newer run shadows an older run for the same id.

EmbeddingModelRequest.description:
Move every embedding of the graph to another model
(`PUT /v1/embeddings/model`). Each embedding builds a new version beside
the serving one; the graph switches to the new model at once when every
embedding has it ready, so a search never mixes two models.

dim.description: The vector dimension; the model's when absent.

iris.description: Show these instances instead of the first ones.

sample.description: Sample entities to show (default 5, at most 50).

EmbeddingPreviewRequest.description:
Preview a declaration (`POST /v1/embeddings/preview`): stores nothing and
calls no model.

candidates.description:
Every field the class could give its text: the recipe's fields first,
then the others by coverage. The automatic choice takes the label,
text facts on at least 10% of the sample, and links to named
entities; values and rarer facts are left for the caller to add.

estimate.description: The spend of embedding every instance, from the samples' mean length.

instances.description: Instances of the class at the published generation.

sampled.description: Instances the candidates were measured on (up to 1,000).

title_suggestion.description:
A fact whose values read as names, when the hits are named by
`rdfs:label` (found or declared) and the labels do not name them (on
less than half of the instances, keys or codes like `yc-job:94386`,
or one value repeated), or the instances have no name. The choice
reads the values, never the property names: a text fact on at least
90% of the sample, about one value per instance, at least 80%
distinct, at most 10% keys or codes, one sentence each, and a median
of at most 120 characters. The most distinct wins, then the shortest.
A suggestion only; the recipe keeps its `title` until a declaration
names another.

EmbeddingRecallStats.description:
Recall of the version's index against an exhaustive search over the same
runs and filter, from sampled searches.

recall_at_k.description: The mean recall@k over the samples.

EmbeddingRecipe.description:
What an embedding embeds and with which model. A change of fields or
model is a new version.

class.description: The class IRI whose instances (`?s a <class>`) are embedded.

title.description:
The path whose value names each hit: one predicate IRI, or a link and
the predicate read on the linked entity. Empty: the instance's
`rdfs:label`. An instance with no value here shows its `rdfs:label`,
else the local name of its IRI.

EmbeddingRunRef.description:
One immutable run of a version: an `lbb-ann` ranged v4 index with a raw
f32 region, and an `ids` table.

bytes.description:
Bytes of the run's objects (meta, blocks, ids); 0 for runs written
before the field existed.

tombstones.description: Ids the run removes from older runs.

text.description:
The exact text the model would embed; empty when the entity has no
value in any field (it gets no vector).

published_lag_commits.description: Commit distance from the graph head to the pinned published generation.

reranked_candidates.description:
Number of candidates re-scored with exact raw-f32 distances. Zero when
`rerank` was not requested or the run has no raw region.

oneOf.description:
Which persisted ANN run served this query relative to the resolved
`as_of` ceiling. Present only when `explain` is set. See
[`SearchTemporalCoverage`].

A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `Eventual`, a floor not yet covered returns a
retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429. `None` == no floor. See
`SearchEngineOptions::min_indexed_seq`.

query_vector.description:
Client-computed query vector. When present it is used directly and the
provider only identifies the embedding space; `query` remains for
display/explain purposes.

rerank.description:
Opt into exact raw-f32 reranking of the persisted vector candidates.
Only effective when the run carries a raw-f32 region (built with
`include_raw`); otherwise it is a no-op. Default off keeps the compact
4-bit-approximate path.

rerank_top_k.description:
How many top approximate candidates to re-score exactly before
truncating to `top_k`. Defaults to a small multiple of `top_k` when
unset; ignored unless `rerank` is set.

lag_commits.description: Commits the serving version is behind the published generation.

oneOf.description: The commit of the published RDF generation now.

EmbeddingStep.description: What one step of the embed job did.

more.description: The version has more work (a backfill page, a fold).

scanned.description: Instances whose text the step rebuilt.

EmbeddingStepTimings.description: Where the time of one job step went, in milliseconds.

embed_ms.description: Reading reused vectors and calling the model.

scan_ms.description:
Finding the instances: the class page, or the commit deltas and the
instances they make dirty.

text_ms.description: Building the texts from the graph.

write_ms.description: Building and writing the run, and the manifest CAS.

EmbeddingTitleSource.description: Where the name of a hit comes from.

EmbeddingUsage.description: Embedding spend. The token count is an estimate: characters / 4.

stored_bytes.description: Bytes the version's runs store (the storage it is billed for).

attributes.description:
The entity's RDF-projected properties as typed JSON: numbers, booleans,
RFC3339 datetime strings, strings and sets. Nulls, bytes, vectors,
non-finite numbers and empty sets have no RDF projection and are omitted.

oneOf.description:
Current RDF relationships. Unlike native edge events, these facts carry
no confidence, valid-time interval, event id or evidence attribution.

Present only when a per-request cap actually cut one of the collections
above, so an ordinary entity's response is byte-identical to the
uncapped one. A supernode read returns the caps' worth of rows plus this
block, rather than its whole degree.

unavailable_sections.description:
Legacy sections unavailable in this read model. An empty listed section
means unavailable, not that the entity has no history or relationships.

EntityDetailTruncation.description:
Which of an entity read's degree-proportional collections were cut, and by
how much. Only the cut collections appear.

oneOf.description:
Set when `outgoing`/`incoming`/`current_state` are a partial view of the
entity's current edges.

truncated_by_read_budget.description:
True when the request's object-read budget stopped the read before its
row caps did, so the counts below are floors for a different reason:
the read gave up rather than the collection being full.

entity_id.description:
Optional resolved entity id (32-char hex). When set, the embedding attaches
to exactly this entity, bypassing `(type, key, name)` resolution. This is
the identity a managed backfill has for each entity it enumerates from a
snapshot — it holds the id but not the original external `key`, which the
id is a one-way hash of, so name-based resolution would create a phantom
name-keyed twin instead of attaching to the keyed entity. `entity_id`
takes precedence over `key`/`name`; `type` is still resolved for the
entity record.

key.description:
Optional stable external key, matching [`NamedEntityInput::key`]. Set it to
attach this embedding to a keyed entity; omit it for `(type, name)`
identity.

oneOf.description: Defaults to Cosine.

attributes.description:
Typed scalar attributes (native JSON), present only when the request asks
for a projection via `?fields=a,b` (or `?fields=*` for all). Lets "list
entities and their titles" be one call instead of a list + N point
lookups. Same `attributes` shape the single-entity read returns.

EntityFieldsWritten.description: The property fields written to one entity by a commit (canonical names).

removed_fields.description:
Previously-stored fields this write **dropped** — present (and non-empty)
only under `property_merge: "replace"`, where the commit's field list
becomes the entity's whole attribute set. Under the default `merge` it is
always empty (a merge never removes a field), so a populated
`removed_fields` is the explicit signal that a destructive replace pruned
attributes the commit did not re-send.

fields.description:
Typed entity properties to return on each matched row. Empty keeps the
lean row; `"*"` or `"all"` projects every property.

filter.description: Property/metadata predicate evaluated against one loaded graph snapshot.

limit.description:
Maximum rows returned. The response's `matched_count` still reports the
full number of matches before this limit is applied.

matched_count.description: Total entities satisfying the predicate before `limit` is applied.

oneOf.description:
Highest commit covered by the **vector/ANN index**, or `None` when no ANN
index has been built. See [`Self::bm25_indexed_commit_seq`].

Highest commit covered by the **BM25 full-text index**, or `None` when no
full-text index has been built. Together with `ann_indexed_commit_seq`
this answers "is this graph indexed for search?" on the dedicated entity
metadata diagnostics read — unlike `snapshot.compacted_seq`, which is the
graph snapshot base. Ordinary entity detail leaves derived-index lineage
absent so a point read never blocks on index discovery. Lag behind
`snapshot.commit_seq` is the unindexed tail.

EntityPropertiesInput.description:
Literal property values to attach to one entity (matched by type + name).

`properties` accepts **two interchangeable shapes**:
- verbose — a list of `{ "field": "...", "value": { "<type>": v } }` objects,
  where `<type>` is one of `bool|i64|f64|date_time|keyword|text`; and
- flat — a `{ "field": value }` object, e.g. `{ "h_index": 52, "title": "VP" }`,
  where the value type is inferred from JSON (bool/integer/float/string) and
  then coerced to the field's declared type at commit (so a flat string lands
  in a `keyword` field, a flat `"2026-06-26"` in a `date_time` field, and a
  flat integer in an `f64` field).

The flat shape removes the nested-`value` ceremony that made `entity_properties`
hard to get right; reach for the verbose shape only when you need to force a
specific wire type.

entity_id.description:
Optional resolved entity id (32-char hex). When set, these properties
attach to exactly this entity, bypassing `(type, key, name)` resolution —
the same escape hatch [`EntityEmbeddingInput::entity_id`] provides. A
managed backfill enumerating a snapshot holds each entity's id but not the
original external `key` (the id is a one-way hash of it), so resolving by
name would attach to — or mint — a phantom name-keyed twin instead of the
real keyed entity. `entity_id` takes precedence over `key`/`name`; `type`
is still resolved for the entity record.

key.description:
Optional stable external key, matching [`NamedEntityInput::key`]. Set it to
attach these properties to a keyed entity; omit it for `(type, name)`
identity.

properties.description:
The field values to write, as a list of `{ "field", "value" }` objects or
as a flat `{ "field": value }` map (see [`PropertiesInput`]).

remove_fields.description:
Field names to **drop** from this entity, applied after `properties` in the
same commit — a surgical per-field delete that avoids a replace-mode
re-send of the whole survivor set (the silent-wipe footgun). Works in
either `property_merge` mode: the named fields are removed from the
entity's stored set even when the rest of the commit merges. A field
listed in both `properties` and `remove_fields` is rejected (you cannot
both set and drop it); an unknown field name is rejected. Dropped fields
are echoed back under `written_properties[].removed_fields`.

EvalAskInput.description:
The inputs of an Ask request (`POST /v1/query/ask`) that shape its
answer, kept on an `ask` trace and its golden so a run asks the same way.
Every field is optional. An object stored before 2026-10-06 may hold
`previous`, the earlier steps of the removed one-shot rewrite: they read
as notes at the end of `context` (the loop reads what the app knows
there), so a follow-up question keeps its meaning when a run asks it
again.

anchor.description: The entity IRIs the user picked (`anchor`).

context.description: The app's notes for the model (`context`).

oneOf.description: The route the caller fixed (`route`).

timeline.description:
The app's own dated points (`timeline`), so a history question finds
the same commits on every run.

today.description:
The date the question was asked (`YYYY-MM-DD`), so a relative
question reads the same window on every run.

EvalItem.description: One result of a query: a hit of a search, or a row of a SPARQL query.

id.description:
Stable id of the result: the term id of a hit; on the `ask` surface
`e:` + the blake3 of the entity IRI the row names, or `v:` + the
blake3 of its values; on the `sparql` surface the blake3 of the
canonical row; `ask:true` / `ask:false` for an ASK answer.

iri.description: The entity the result names, when it names one.

label.description: A short display form: the hit's label, or the row's values.

rank.description: Position in the returned list, from 0.

value.description: The result as returned: a SPARQL binding row, or a hit.

id.description: The result id (`id` on a hit or a trace item).

valid.description: True: the result answers the request (thumbs up).

EvalItems.description: The results a query returned, in a form that compares across commits.

items.description: The first [`EVAL_INLINE_ITEM_LIMIT`] results, in returned order.

items_blake3.description: blake3 over the sorted result ids: the set, not the order.

rejected.description: Results the judge labeled not relevant.

review.description: Results the judge left for a person.

model.description: The model behind the provider, when it has one.

by.description: Free-form labeler identity (an agent name, a user id, a judge model).

probability.description: The judge's probability that the result answers the request.

valid.description: True: the result answers the request (thumbs up).

EvalLabelRequest.description:
Thumbs up or down on results of a trace: one result as `item` + `valid`,
or several in `items`. On an `ask` trace, `valid` without `item` or
`items` labels the answer as a whole: `true` makes the trace's query the
golden query of the question; `false` with `sparql` makes that query the
golden query (the server checks and runs it once); `false` alone marks
the answer wrong.

oneOf.description: `explicit` (default) or `implicit`. `judge` is reserved for the server.

sparql.description: With `valid: false` and no `item`: the right query for the question.

oneOf.description: The golden that now holds the labels.

EvalMode.description:
Where evals run. `Off` records traces and goldens but never runs them on
its own; `Advisory` runs them on demand and on the periodic tick. A
blocking gate is not part of this increment.

EvalQueryCheck.description:
The query check of an `ask` golden: the rows of the query Ask wrote
against the rows of the golden query, both read at the same commit. It
passes when `missing` and `extra` are 0.

extra.description: Rows only the written query returns.

missing.description: Rows only the golden query returns.

EvalQueryType.description: The type of a question's query.

EvalResults.description: One run of the suite at one commit of the graph. One object per commit.

cost_micro_usd.description:
What the models of the run's Ask replays cost together, in
millionths of a US dollar; absent when the run asked nothing.

goldens_version.description: The suite version the run read.

precision.description: Mean precision over the goldens with judged results returned.

recall.description: Mean recall over the goldens with known-relevant results.

regression.description: True when `score` is below the settings threshold.

review_traces.description: Traces this run opened for results nobody judged yet.

score.description: Share of goldens that pass; `1.0` for an empty suite.

max_goldens.description: Goldens the runner executes per run, at most [`EVAL_HARD_MAX_GOLDENS`].

threshold.description: Score below which a run is reported as a regression.

review_traces.description: Traces with results the judge left for a person.

unlabeled_items.description: Results nobody labeled yet, across those traces.

unlabeled_traces.description: Traces with a result nobody labeled yet, among the most recent traces.

EvalSurface.description: Which surface a trace or a golden belongs to.

oneOf.description:
The answer label of an `ask` trace: its query is right for the
question (`valid: true`), or it is wrong.

The inputs of the Ask request, for an `ask` trace of
`POST /v1/query/rewrite`.

golden_id.description: The golden that holds this trace's labels.

judged_at.description: RFC 3339; set when the judge looked at the trace.

oneOf.description: The type of the query, for an `ask` trace.

What Ask answered in words, with the IRIs it cited: on the trace of
`POST /v1/query/ask`, and on a run's review trace of an `ask`
golden. An answer label judges it with the query.

request.description: The user's words, as the caller passed them in `request`.

review.description:
Results the judge looked at but left for a person, with its
probability (between the two thresholds).

served_at_seq.description: The commit of the graph the results were read at.

sparql.description: The SPARQL query, or the query text on the vector surface.

v.description: Trace format version. Currently `2`: labels per result.

cost_micro_usd.description:
What the models of the replay cost, in millionths of a US dollar
(`via: ask`).

oneOf.description: The type the golden expects (`ask` goldens).

precision.description:
`relevant_returned / (relevant_returned + wrong_returned)`, over the
judged results that came back.

oneOf.description:
The query check (`ask` goldens of type `sparql` or `hybrid` with a
golden query). The result counts above are the result check against
the judged results.
The type of the query that ran this time (`ask` goldens).

relevant_missing.description: Known-relevant results that did not come back.

oneOf.description:
What Ask answered this time in words, with the IRIs it cited
(`via: ask`). The run checks the rows; it reports the words.

review_trace_id.description: The trace opened for the unknown results (the review queue).

oneOf.description: The route of the question this time (`via: ask`).

sparql.description: The query Ask wrote this time (`via: ask`).

oneOf.description: How the run tested the golden; absent when it was skipped.

EvalVia.description: How a run tested a golden.

observation_id.description:
Stable observation id used by full-fidelity export/import. Ordinary
callers omit it and receive the existing deterministic request id.

oneOf.description:
Optional page-region anchor for this evidence. Requires `text`
(the region anchors to the evidence observation the text creates).

ExtractorDatasetResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/extractor-dataset` — the extractor fine-tune's training
feed: stored `EPISODE` transcripts joined (via evidence observations) to
the facts the observe pipeline committed from them, plus the ontology
vocabulary the serving prompt carries (so the trainer rebuilds the exact
extraction prompt).

relations.description: The extraction prompt's relation vocabulary at this snapshot.

split_seq.description: Facts with commit seq ≤ this were consumed.

types.description: The extraction prompt's entity-type vocabulary at this snapshot.

ExtractorExample.description:
One extractor training example: an episode transcript and the facts that
were actually committed from it.

ExtractorFact.description:
One extractor training fact, mirroring the resident extractor's strict
output JSON (`{statement, source_type, source, relation, target_type,
target, confidence}`) — every committed fact was vocabulary-snapped
before it was committed, so labels are execution-verified.

FlatPropertyValue.description:
A bare JSON value in the flat `{ field: value }` property shape: a boolean,
an integer, a number, a string, or an array of integers or of strings. The
wire type is inferred from JSON; the commit path coerces it to the field's
declared `PropertyType`, so the inferred variant only needs to be in the
right ballpark.

published_lag_commits.description: Commit distance from the graph head to the pinned published generation.

oneOf.description:
Which immutable run in the pinned published generation served this
query. Present only when `explain` is set. See
[`SearchTemporalCoverage`].

A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `Eventual`, a floor not yet covered returns a
retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429. `None` == no floor. See
`SearchEngineOptions::min_indexed_seq`.

offset.description:
Number of leading results to skip after ordering, for stateless paging:
`offset = page * top_k` walks pages deterministically. Defaults to 0.
Paging operates over a bounded candidate pool (~16 × `top_k`), not the
full match set, so paging is lossy past that pool: an `offset` beyond the
pool returns an empty page and documents outside the pool are omitted.
Keep `top_k` large enough that the pages you need fall inside the pool.

order.description:
Sort direction for `order_by`. Defaults to descending (highest score /
metadata value first).

order_by.description:
Ordering key for the result page. Defaults to relevance score. Ties
always break on the stable document id so paging is deterministic.
Ordering is applied over the bounded candidate pool (~16 × `top_k`), so
`order_by: metadata` reorders the top-scoring slice rather than the full
match set — matches outside the pool are not considered.

FusionServingDefaults.description:
Fusion serving default derived from a promoted `fusion` run: the weights
the search path applies when a request neither overrides the field nor
pins an explicit retrieval profile.

run.description: The promoted registry run these weights came from.

accepted_at.description: RFC 3339; set when the current results were accepted as the reference.

accepted_by.description: Who accepted the last change: `user` or the judge provider.

oneOf.description:
The answer label that made `sparql` the golden query of an `ask`
golden (who, when). Absent: `sparql` is the query of the newest
labeled trace, and the run checks the judged results.

The inputs a run asks an `ask` golden's question with, from the
newest labeled trace.

frozen_at_seq.description: The commit the judgments were last changed at.

id.description:
blake3 of the request words, the query text and entailment (plus
embedding and `top_k` for a search), so a regenerated or
re-added golden keeps its identity and its trend. An `ask` golden
keys on the question alone: its words, its sorted anchors and a
digest of its earlier steps.

judgments.description: The judged results by id: the ground truth.

oneOf.description:
The type of query an `ask` golden expects: the type of its golden
query, else of the newest labeled trace's query.

trace_ids.description: The most recent traces that labeled into this golden (bounded).

v.description: Golden format version. Currently `2`: judgments per result.

sparql.description:
The SPARQL query, or the query text for `surface: search`. Freezes a
`sparql` or a `search` golden; a question becomes an `ask` golden
through a label on its trace.

GoldenJudgment.description: What a golden knows about one result.

relevant.description:
True: the result answers the request and must keep being returned.
False: the result is wrong and must not come back.

GoldenSuite.description: The suite: one CAS-versioned document per graph.

GraphActivityResponse.description:
The background work on one graph epoch, as `GET /v1/graph/activity`
reports it.

head_seq.description: The newest commit written to the graph.

idle.description:
True when no item is queued, waiting or running, `publication` is
`current`, and every embedding is `ready` with `lag_commits` 0 or
`failed` (a failed embedding waits for a fix, so no work runs).

items.description:
Queued, waiting and running items first, then finished items. Newest
first in each group. At most 25.

observed_at_micros.description:
Server clock when the route read the state (micros since the Unix
epoch).

published_seq.description:
The newest commit the published RDF generation covers (queries see
it). 0 before the first generation.

target_seq.description: The commit the publication works toward.

write_limit.description:
How close the unpublished commits are to the limit at which the
server refuses new writes (retryable `429 ingest_busy`) until the
index catches up.

GraphAnchor.description:
A structural co-bind constraint: restrict (or boost) the text/vector
candidates to entities within an anchor entity's relation-neighborhood. This
is the engine-native form of the query-conditional channel routing validated
in the Stage-G ablation (quality-ledger R17) — "documents about X AND in the
same group as Y" becomes one snapshot-consistent search rather than a blind
list fusion. The neighborhood is computed from the snapshot-reduced Base
family; final candidates are still re-verified against snapshot visibility.

anchor.description: The anchor entity to expand from.

hops.description: Neighborhood radius in hops (clamped to a small bound; default 2).

oneOf.description: `filter` (hard JOIN) or `boost` (soft). Defaults to `filter`.

relation.description:
Restrict the neighborhood walk to this relation type (by name). `None`
follows every relation.

GraphBindMode.description: How a graph anchor co-binds with the text/vector channels.

GraphCard.description:
WS3 — a per-graph, per-snapshot self-description an agent can inject as prompt
context: the types, relations, properties, and top attribute values that
actually exist, with counts and a freshness watermark. The database writes
its own guaranteed-true few-shot examples. Computed from the ontology,
resident overlay, and BM25 meta — no doc/postings reads — and bounded by
`limits` so it stays small enough to prompt with.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
The last commit written at or before the moment. Absent when the
server cannot place it: `note` says why.

committed_at.description:
When that commit was written, RFC 3339; absent when it records no
time.

first_commit_at.description:
The moment is before the graph's first commit: when that commit was
written (or the graph created), RFC 3339.

moment.description: The moment asked about, RFC 3339 UTC: the end of `date`, or `moment`.

note.description: Why there is no commit, or what to know about the one found.

GraphCommitDryRunResponse.description:
The result of a validate-only commit (`POST /v1/graph/commit?dry_run=true`):
the request is fully validated against the ontology and the active schema and
the would-be effect is reported, but nothing is persisted. A 4xx here is the
same validation error a real commit would raise (unknown type/relation,
unregistered property field, type mismatch), so it is a safe ETL preflight.

dry_run.description: Always true — marks this as a non-persisting preflight.

op_count.description: Number of WAL ops the commit would produce.

oneOf.description:
Active-schema SHACL audit of the prospective commit, when a shape bundle
is active. `conforms=false` means a `reject`-mode commit would be blocked.

skipped_edges.description: Edges that would be skipped as unchanged (idempotent no-ops).

triplets.description: Triplets that would be written, after idempotent skip-unchanged filtering.

written_properties.description:
Property fields that would be written, per entity (canonical names),
resolved against the ontology — the same echo a real commit returns.

drain_pressure.description:
R27d(1) advisory WAL drain pressure (0.0–1.0), mirrored from
`commit.drain_pressure`. Present only once the tail is over half full.

replayed.description:
Top-level replay signal for idempotency-key collisions/retries. Mirrors
`commit.idempotent_replay` so callers do not have to unwrap the commit
envelope before deciding whether anything new was written.

throttle_ms.description:
R27d(1) advisory pacing telemetry, mirrored from `commit.throttle_ms` to
the envelope top level (like `replayed`) and to the `X-LBB-Throttle-Ms`
response header. Present only past a noise floor; clients SHOULD reduce
write concurrency as it rises.

written_properties.description:
Top-level echo of property fields actually written by this request.
Empty on idempotent replays and no-ops.

deleted_feedback_objects.description:
Always 0: search feedback is reclaimed in the background with the
rest of the graph.

deleted_objects.description:
Objects the request itself removed (the workflow state and history
of the deleted graph). The rest is reclaimed in the background; see
`reclaims`.

reclaims.description:
The background passes that reclaim the deleted graph's storage, one
per branch. Empty when reclaim is turned off on the server.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
Pin the export to a past snapshot: only entities, assertions, and
observations committed at or before this `commit_seq` are emitted. A pin
past the current head is rejected loudly (never clamped), matching the
graph read paths. `None` exports the latest head. This is what makes a
long-running training run's export reproducible — resolve the head once,
then pin every subsequent read to the same `commit_seq` so an N+1 commit
mid-run can never change the training corpus.

snapshot_token.description:
Opaque, self-describing token for the exact snapshot this export reflects
(`tenant:graph:branch:epoch:commit_seq`). Records the exported snapshot's
provenance so a caller can pin subsequent reads to — and verify
reproducibility against — the same point in history.

GraphForkResponse.description:
Response to `POST /v1/graph/fork`: the fork runs as a durable background job
(a create-only copy of the source graph into a new graph id in the same
tenant), so this acknowledges the enqueue and points at the poll surface.

poll.description:
Poll the destination graph's metadata to observe the fork completing
(the destination becomes readable once its head is published).

GraphImportJobAccepted.description: Stable response returned when a durable import is accepted or replayed.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this request resolved to an existing job with the same
idempotency key and exact content hash.

GraphImportJobFailure.description:
Terminal failure details for a durable import. The message is safe to expose
to the submitting client; internal object keys and worker identities stay in
structured server logs.

attempts.description: Delivery attempts consumed when the job became terminal.

diagnostic_id.description:
Stable opaque correlation id for server-side logs. It is intentionally
not an object key, worker id, or graph identity.

stage.description: Last durable low-cardinality stage reached by the worker.

GraphImportJobProgress.description: Bounded progress persisted by an import worker after every grouped commit.

GraphImportJobStage.description: Low-cardinality execution stage exposed while a durable import is active.

GraphImportJobState.description:
Lifecycle of a durable NDJSON import submitted through
`POST /v1/graph/import-jobs`.

A succeeded import has durably committed its records and enqueued the final
publication job. It does **not** mean the published read generation has
already caught up to [`GraphImportJobStatus::committed_commit_seq`].

GraphImportJobStatus.description: Queryable status for a durable import job.

oneOf.description:
Final publication enqueue receipt. Presence means publication was
accepted, not that published reads have caught up.

GraphImportLine.description:
One line of an NDJSON bulk-import stream (`POST /v1/graph/import`). Each line
is a single JSON object that is either a triplet (carries `relation`) or an
entity-properties record (carries `properties`); the two shapes are disjoint,
so the importer routes each line by shape. This is the streamable counterpart
of `TripletCommitFile`: a client streams a large dataset line-by-line instead
of buffering one giant commit, and the server batches lines into bounded
internal commits.

GraphImportLineError.description:
A per-line parse/commit failure surfaced by the bulk importer. `line` is the
1-based NDJSON line number. The importer records these and continues (skip the
bad line), unless `strict` is requested.

GraphImportPublishedGenerationOutcome.description:
Durable publication accepted after `POST /v1/graph/import`.
The import request never constructs index families or waits for publication;
clients can poll the returned job while continuing to observe the previously
published generation.

GraphImportResponse.description:
Aggregate outcome of a bulk NDJSON import. `committed_commit_seq` is the
sequence of the last internal batch commit (absent if nothing committed).
`errors` is bounded; `error_count` is the true total even when the list is
truncated. `published_generation` is present when at least one batch
committed; publication is automatic.

idempotency_key.description: The caller key, or the server-minted key when the caller omitted one.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when every internal mutation batch was the already-committed
receipt for this idempotency key.

mutation_receipt_id.description:
Stable identity for the whole multi-batch mutation. Replays return this
exact receipt and the original terminal commit sequence.

observations.description: Exact observation records imported from a full-fidelity export.

GraphListResponse.description: The live, head-backed graphs under a tenant (one stack in SaaS mode).

index_caught_up.description:
One-shot "has the published generation caught up to head?" signal, so a
bulk-import caller does not hand-assemble the predicate.
`Some(true)` iff the published generation is served at the head commit;
`Some(false)` when publication is still pending or absent; `None` when
indexes were not inspected (`include_indexes=false`).

This is a **publication lag** signal, not a statement about index
content. A generation whose BM25/ANN families are published as empty
roots — the steady state when the deployment runs without the search
stack — is caught up while holding no documents. Read
`index_lineage.bm25_empty` / `ann_empty` to tell the two apart.

published_lag_commits.description: Commit distance from the graph head to the pinned published generation.

segment_count.description: Compacted snapshot segments referenced by the graph manifest.

GraphRdfImportError.description:
A bounded parse error from RDF bulk import. The RDF parser reports syntax
positions in its message, so this type keeps the wire shape honest instead of
pretending there is always a recoverable line number.

GraphRdfImportPredicate.description:
A predicate discovered while importing RDF through `POST /v1/graph/import/rdf`.
`uri` is the original RDF predicate IRI. `relation` is the fixed
`RDF_TRIPLE` relation used for committed edges, while `lbb_predicate_iri`
remains the source predicate IRI that the RDF/SPARQL projection emits.

GraphRdfImportResponse.description:
Aggregate outcome of an RDF import. Every RDF statement is committed
through a fixed `RDF_TRIPLE` edge; source predicate and literal term metadata
are stored on the edge so the RDF/SPARQL projection can emit source RDF terms
while avoiding one ontology relation/property per source predicate.

GraphReclaimSchedule.description: A background pass that reclaims the storage of a deleted graph branch.

mode.description: `apply` deletes; `plan` only counts what a pass would delete.

not_before.description: RFC 3339. The pass does not start before this time.

GraphReloadResponse.description:
Outcome of `POST /v1/graph/reload` — the declarative "make the graph match
this full dataset" verb. One atomic cutover replaces the whole current state:
records present in the payload are upserted, and entities present at the
pre-reload head but absent from the payload are removed from current state
(retraction semantics — history stays queryable via `?as_of_commit_seq=`).
The delta report is the "prove I don't have wrong data" aid.

The whole reconciliation lands as a single graph-head advance, so a reader
never observes a mixed old/new state: a snapshot pinned at `prior_commit_seq`
sees only the old state, and `new_commit_seq` sees only the new state, with
nothing in between.

dry_run.description:
True when this was a `?dry_run=true` preview: nothing durable changed and
the counts + `new_commit_seq`/`new_snapshot_token` are the *proposed*
effect of a real reload against the same pre-reload head.

edges_added.description: Payload edges not currently present, within the reconciled scopes.

edges_changed.description: Payload edges already present (re-asserted), within the reconciled scopes.

edges_removed.description: Current edges retracted because an endpoint left current state.

entities_added.description: Entities present in the payload but not at the pre-reload head.

entities_changed.description:
Entities present in both the payload and the pre-reload head (re-asserted;
this is a presence intersection, not a deep property diff).

entities_removed.description:
Entities present at the pre-reload head but absent from the payload — the
ones leaving current state.

error_count.description:
Parse errors for malformed payload lines (bounded; `error_count` is the
true total). Mirrors bulk import.

graph_created.description:
True when the target graph did not exist and this reload bootstrapped it
(the pre-reload baseline was empty).

idempotency_key.description:
The idempotency key that scopes this reload's single commit (the caller
key, or a server-minted one).

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this request id was already applied (idempotent replay): the
diff counts are reported as zero because nothing new was written.

new_commit_seq.description:
Commit sequence after cutover (real), or the proposed next sequence (dry
run).

new_snapshot_token.description: Snapshot token after cutover (real), or the proposed token (dry run).

no_op.description:
True when the desired state already matched the current state and no
commit was written (real mode only).

prior_commit_seq.description:
Commit sequence of the pre-reload head — the diff baseline and the
rollback anchor.

prior_snapshot_token.description:
Snapshot token of the pre-reload head. Read it back with
`?as_of_commit_seq=<prior_commit_seq>` to see the old state — the rollback
hint.

removed_sample.description:
A bounded sample of the entities leaving current state, as `type/name`
display identities (external keys are one-way-hashed and unrecoverable) —
a sanity aid for confirming the reload drops what you expect.

GraphRetractRequest.description:
Retract specific edges and/or every edge touching given entities. Graph facts
are append-only; a retraction does not erase events but appends a retracting
event that supersedes the matched current edges, so they drop out of
current-state reads (and re-appear in an `as_of` read before the retraction).
This is the surgical alternative to the whole-graph reset for fixing a
wrongly-added fact — e.g. an auto-extracted entity that turned out to be noise.

edges.description:
Specific edges to retract, matched against current edges by
(source, relation, target).

entities.description:
Entities whose every current edge (as source or target) is retracted —
effectively tombstoning the entity from current-state reads. The entity
record itself is retained (append-only) and stays visible in `as_of` reads.

purge_entity_properties.description:
Also clear every stored scalar property (`text`, `acl`, …) of each entity
in `entities`, so the entity has **no current presence** and fully leaves
search AND SPARQL in this one call — the "delete this record" primitive.
Without it, `retract` tombstones edges only; a property-carrying entity
(e.g. a content chunk with an `acl`) stays searchable and ACL-filterable
because presence is `live-edge OR non-empty properties`. Append-only: the
records survive in `as_of` reads; only the current property set is cleared
(a later `commit` can repopulate it). No-op for `edges`-only requests.

edge_event_ids.description: The retracting edge-event ids appended by this request.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this request id was already applied (idempotent replay); counts
are reported as zero because nothing new was written.

no_op.description: True when nothing matched, so no event was written.

purged_entities.description:
Entities (from `entities`) whose stored properties were cleared by
`purge_entity_properties`. Zero when the flag is unset.

retracted_edges.description: Distinct current edges retracted by this request.

retracted_entities.description: Entities (from `entities`) that had at least one current edge retracted.

GroundabilityReport.description:
WS13 — a graph's self-reported groundability: per graph, which completion
mechanisms will carry. Turns the campaign's hand measurements into a
self-service report so a caller can pick narrowing / fine-tuning /
lexical-first without running the experiment.

IdentityMember.description: One record of a [`SuggestedIdentity`], by its import identity.

key.description: Its stable import key (for an integration, `<connection>:<stream>:<id>`).

name.description:
Its current display name. The `SAME_AS` edge names both endpoints, so
a different name would rename the record.

source.description: Display text for the source, for example `hubspot-main contacts`.

IndexLineage.description: Typed convergence view over the persisted serving families.

ann_empty.description:
True when the published ANN family is an empty root. Same meaning as
`bm25_empty`.

oneOf.description:
Watermark the published ANN family is served at. Same caveat as
`bm25_indexed_commit_seq`; read `ann_empty` alongside it.

bm25_empty.description:
True when the published BM25 family is an empty root — the deployment
runs without the search stack
(`LBB_PUBLISH_EMPTY_INDEX_FAMILIES`), or the corpus genuinely has no
indexable documents at this watermark. Either way the family is current
*and* contains nothing, so a health check must not read `caught_up`
alone as "search is serving results".

oneOf.description:
Watermark the published BM25 family is served at. This reports
*publication currency*, not index content: a family published as a
self-identifying empty root is current at this watermark while
containing no documents. Read `bm25_empty` alongside it.

caught_up.description:
Both families are published at the head commit. This is a *publication
lag* signal — it says the derived families have caught up with graph
truth, not that they hold data. An empty family is caught up.

manifest_view_token.description:
Content identity of the head generation plus the exact manifest
views observed while constructing this response.

current_tables.description:
Tables already carrying this accelerator format. This does not promise
expression coverage for every predicate or every query shape.

Extractor adapter serving default (a LoRA adapter on the resident
model's volume); resident extraction passes it per generate call.

`GET /v1/models/split-audit` — makes the WS9 temporal-split obligation
checkable: a trainer MUST train on data ≤ `trained_at_commit_seq` and

The lineage window closes at or before the split pin
(`signal_to_seq ≤ trained_at_commit_seq`).

Per-graph automatic-training configuration, stored as one small CAS
object under the graph prefix (purged with the tenant). **[PIN]** field

Which [`TRAINABLE_KINDS`] the cadence loop may train. Empty with
`auto_train: true` means "all trainable kinds".

Whether entity names look like natural language (embeddings will carry) or
opaque identifiers (a hash/lexical approach fits better).

sampled.description: Entity names sampled for the heuristic.

key.description:
Optional stable external key. When set, entity identity is `(type, key)`
and `name` is just a display label — so a later rename keeps the same
entity, and two records that share a name stay distinct by key (e.g. two
"Cambridge" universities in a relational import). Omit it to keep the
default `(type, name)` identity. To attach properties or embeddings to a
keyed entity, set the same `key` on those inputs.

NarrowRelationOp.description:
Remove entity types from a relation's domain and/or range (a subtractive
change). Conflicts when current edges of the relation already use a
removed source/target type — those edges stay (append-only) but begin to
warn. Blocked until those edges are migrated or retracted.

NarrowingRecall.description:
Whether the graph's own entities are retrievable by their names — a proxy
for "will narrowing/retrieval carry". Computed by self-querying a sample and
checking top-10 membership; no LLM.

OntologyChangeSuggestion.description: A durable, reviewable ontology change suggestion.

accepted_links.description: How many `SAME_AS` edges the accept wrote.

accepted_ontology_version.description: The ontology version the accepted change produced.

change.description:
The evolve operations that accepting applies, in order. May be empty
when `identities` is not.

change_sources.description:
For an edited change: for each op of `change`, the index of the op in
`proposed_change` it was edited from, or null for an op the person
added. Lets a producer map its proposal onto what was accepted.

decided_by.description: Who accepted, dismissed or superseded it, when, and why.

identities.description: Records to link as one identity after `change` applies.

oneOf.description:
The last dry run of `change` against the ontology, or the result of
accepting it. `impact.base_ontology_version` below the graph's current
ontology version means the dry run is out of date.

impact_error.description: Why the last dry run failed (for example an unknown class).

key.description:
The producer's idempotency key. Creating again with the same key
updates this suggestion instead of adding another one.

mapping.description:
Opaque to the server: how the origin applies the change to its own
configuration once accepted (for an integration, its mapping changes).

proposed_change.description:
The operations as the producer proposed them, kept when a person edited
`change` before accepting.

proposed_identities.description:
The identities as the producer proposed them, kept when a person
removed some before accepting.

revision.description: Starts at 1 and grows each time the producer revises the change.

OntologyChangeSuggestionAcceptRequest.description:
Accept a suggestion: apply its change to the current ontology, then link
its identities.

change.description: An edited change that replaces the proposed one ("edit, then accept").

change_sources.description:
With `change`: for each of its ops, the index of the proposed op it was
edited from, or null for an added op. Same length as `change`; each
index at most once.

comment.description: Added to the discussion with the acceptance.

identities.description:
The identities to link, when a person removed some or some members:
each must be a subset of a proposed identity, with at least two
members. Absent links every proposed identity.

OntologyChangeSuggestionCommentRequest.description: Add a comment to a suggestion's discussion.

OntologyChangeSuggestionCreateRequest.description:
Create a suggestion, or update the one with the same `key`.

Update rules for an existing key: an `open` suggestion takes the new
content (a different `change` raises `revision`); an `accepted` one is
returned unchanged; a `dismissed` one stays dismissed unless `change`
differs, which reopens it; a `superseded` one reopens.

oneOf.description: Defaults to the ontology as a whole.

change.description:
Up to 128 evolve operations; at least one unless `identities` is set
(then it may be empty).

identities.description: Up to 200 identities to link on accept.

key.description:
Idempotency key, at most 255 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9-_.:/]`, for
example `hubspot-main/deals`. When absent the server derives one from
`anchor`, `change` and (when set) `identities`, so the same suggestion
is filed once.

mapping.description: Opaque origin data, at most 16 KiB of JSON.

rationale.description: Why the change is needed. At most 4,000 characters.

title.description:
Short imperative text, for example "Add class Deal". At most 200
characters.

OntologyChangeSuggestionDecisionRequest.description: Dismiss (a person) or supersede (the producer) a suggestion.

OntologyChangeSuggestionStatus.description: Where a suggestion is in its review.

OntologyChangeSuggestionSummary.description:
One row of a suggestion list: everything but the evidence samples, the
mapping and the discussion text.

identity_count.description: How many identities the suggestion links.

publishable.description: Whether the last dry run can be published; absent before any dry run.

OntologyConflict.description:
A current-data conflict found while previewing a subtractive ontology change.
Reported back so the caller can decide whether to re-run with
`allow_data_conflicts` (which keeps the affected records — Little Big Brain never
rewrites or drops them — and applies the change in warn mode).

affected.description: How many current records the change would orphan/flag.

samples.description: Bounded deterministic examples. `affected` remains the exact count.

OntologyDefineRequest.description:
Define the scoped graph's ontology. Imports `source` (any
[`crate`]-supported format), optionally merges the built-in default so the
standard entity types/relations stay available, and creates the graph head
with the result.

The call is re-runnable on a graph that already exists. An unchanged
ontology is a no-op; an additive difference is applied, including a widened
relation domain or range and a new property field; a narrowing or removing
difference is refused with a typed error naming the route that applies it.

dry_run.description:
Preview the exact definition without creating a graph, writing an
ontology object, or changing the graph head. Equivalent to the
`?dry_run=true` query parameter; either signal enables preview mode.

format.description: Import format hint. `auto` (the default) sniffs the content.

merge_default.description:
Merge the built-in `default_ai_context_ontology()` underneath the
imported types so the standard AI-context vocabulary stays available.

source.description:
Ontology document text: Little Big Brain JSON, JSON-LD, Turtle/N3, RDF/XML, or
CSV/TSV. Detected from `format` (default `auto`).

changed.description:
True when this call wrote a new ontology version, or when a dry run
predicts that it would. False when the proposed ontology already matched
the active one, which is what makes re-running the same bootstrap request
a no-op.

A widened relation domain or range and a new property field both set it,
even though neither appears in the class-and-relation schema diff.

changes.description:
The additive changes this call applied, or would apply during a dry run,
to an existing graph's ontology. Empty on create and no-op.

dry_run.description: True when this response is a preview and no durable state changed.

graph_created.description:
True when this call created the graph head, or when a dry run predicts
that the real definition would create it.

OntologyDraft.description: Durable, portable ontology review artifact owned by the graph database.

OntologyDraftCreateRequest.description: Create a reviewable induction artifact without inserting samples into the graph.

OntologyEntityTypeView.description: The full definition of one entity type (class) in the active ontology.

iri.description: Canonical query IRI minted by Little Big Brain for this class identity.

resolvable.description: True when instances of this type can be resolved from free-text mentions.

stable_id.description:
Frozen class identity used by commits and the RDF projection. This is
unique even when imported vocabularies reuse the same local name.

super_types.description:
Direct parent classes (`rdfs:subClassOf`), named by their frozen
`stable_id`s. Clients can build the full class lattice without a SPARQL
scan or a second ontology lookup.

evidence_ref.description: Stable connector/source reference; sample content is never used as identity.

record.description:
Representative connector record. Objects enable deterministic property
inference; other JSON values remain evidence examples.

OntologyEvolveOp.description:
One additive ontology change for [`OntologyEvolveRequest`]. Additive by
construction — it widens a relation's domain/range or declares a new entity
type, but never narrows or removes — so every record written under an earlier
version stays valid (its positional type/relation ids are preserved). This is
the supported "ontology evolution" path; identity-breaking changes (removals,
narrowing) still require an explicit expand→migrate→contract plan.

Every variant rejects unknown fields: a misspelled field fails the request
with `400 invalid_request` instead of reading as an empty change.

OntologyEvolveRequest.description:
Apply a list of additive ontology changes in order, writing a new ontology
version when anything actually changes. Ops are applied against the
in-progress ontology, so an `add_entity_type` earlier in the list is visible
to a later `widen_relation`.

allow_data_conflicts.description:
Deprecated compatibility field. Conflicting subtractive changes are
always rejected with structured conflicts until affected data is
migrated or retracted; setting this field no longer bypasses that gate.

applied.description:
The changes actually applied (empty on a no-op, or when a conflicting
subtractive request was rejected without `allow_data_conflicts`).

conflicts.description:
Current-data conflicts from subtractive ops. When non-empty and the
request did not set `allow_data_conflicts`, nothing was written and
`ontology_version` is unchanged.

dry_run.description:
True when this response came from `?dry_run=true` and no ontology object
or graph-head update was written.

no_op.description:
Every requested operation was already satisfied, so publishing would not
create a new ontology version.

ontology_version.description:
Active version after a publish, or the predicted resulting version for a
dry run. Equal to `base_ontology_version` for a no-op or blocked preview.

publishable.description:
Whether the exact request can be published. False for every
data-conflicting subtractive preview.

OntologyPropertyView.description: A typed property on an entity type, as declared in the active ontology.

allowed_values.description:
The field's enforced allowed-value set (`sh:in`), if any — a commit whose
value is outside it is rejected at write time. Empty/absent means the
field accepts any value of its type.

value_type.description:
Lowercase value type: bool | i64 | f64 | datetime | keyword | text |
bytes | vector_f32 | keyword_set | i64_set. The `*_set` types hold a
sorted, deduplicated member set filterable by membership
(`overlaps`/`contains_all`/`not_overlaps`).

OntologyRelationView.description:
The full definition of one relation type (predicate) in the active ontology,
with domain/range resolved to entity-type names so the schema renders without
a second lookup.

dst_types.description: Range — entity-type names this relation can point to (empty = any).

edge_count.description:
Number of current (reduced) edges of this relation in the served snapshot,
when the caller asked for population counts (`GET /v1/ontology?counts=true`).
`0` flags a declared-but-unused relation; `None` (field omitted) means the
count was not requested — the default cheap response skips the snapshot
load. Lets an agent see at a glance which of many declared relations
actually carry edges.

src_types.description: Domain — entity-type names this relation can originate from (empty = any).

exact_types.description:
When false (default), an `entity_types` constraint is satisfied by the
named type *or any subtype* (`rdfs:subClassOf` closure). When true, only
the exact declared type matches — the exact-match escape hatch.

widened_relations.description:

range classes.

status.description: The starter's status after the call, or the predicted one in a dry run.

A class of a starter. LBB does not scope properties to classes:
`properties` is a hint for the fit and the docs.

equivalents.description: Equivalent or closest terms in public vocabularies, as CURIEs.

keys.description:
Properties whose value identifies one real thing across sources. No
ontology operation holds them yet.

properties.description:
The properties records of this class carry, beyond its parents' and
the shared ones.

superTypes.description: Direct parents, declared earlier in the starter.

A term the graph holds differently from the starter. Applying would keep
the graph's version silently, so `apply` refuses while one exists.

name.description: The term's name in the starter.

starter.description:
What the starter declares, for example `keyword` or
`many_to_one, inverse EMPLOYS`.

OntologyStarterConflictKind.description: The kind of term a conflict is about.

OntologyStarterDetail.description:
`GET /v1/ontology/starters/detail`: one starter's document, its status and

missing_ops.description:
The evolve operations applying the starter would run now: what the
graph lacks, with a relation the graph has widened instead of added.

ontology_version.description: Null when the graph does not exist yet.

A starter as the JSON document the data plane embeds
(`database/crates/lbb-ontology/starters/<id>.json`).

ops.description: The evolve operations that create the starter on an empty graph.

shared.description: Properties every record of every class may carry (provenance).

sources.description: The connector kinds that map to this starter, for example `hubspot`.

version.description: Semantic version. A major change renames or removes terms.

OntologyStarterList.description: `GET /v1/ontology/starters`: every starter with its status on the graph.

ontology_version.description:
The graph's ontology version; null when the graph does not exist yet
(every starter is then `absent`).

OntologyStarterPresent.description: How many of a starter's terms the graph holds.

OntologyStarterProperty.description: A property of a starter. Properties are global: one name, one value type.

equivalent.description: The schema.org (or other) term it corresponds to, as a CURIE.

OntologyStarterQuestion.description:
A question the starter's ontology must answer, with the terms an answer
needs.

sparql.description: The SPARQL that answers it, when one exists.

domain.description: Class names the relation goes from.

inverse.description: The name of the reverse direction.

range.description: Class names the relation goes to.

OntologyStarterState.description: How much of a starter a graph holds.

OntologyStarterStatus.description: A starter compared with a graph's ontology.

OntologyStarterUpdateRequest.description:
File the operations a graph lacks of a starter as one ontology change
suggestion.

OntologyStarterUpdateResponse.description: The suggestion a starter update filed.

created.description:
True when this call filed the suggestion; false when it existed
already (it may have been revised) or nothing was needed.

suggestion_id.description: The suggestion's id; null when the graph already holds the starter.

OntologyTermView.description:
A named entity type or relation in the graph's active ontology. Returned by
the define and read-ontology routes so tenants can confirm the vocabulary in
effect for commits.

concept_count.description: Count of named concepts in the ontology's semantic layer.

decoration_status.description:
Engine-global catalog of which decorations are enforced/advisory/reserved
(see [`decoration_catalog`]). Identical for every graph; lets clients show
honestly what the engine acts on versus merely records.

entity_type_defs.description: Full entity-type definitions (properties, resolvability, version range).

property_defs.description:
The graph's **global** typed-property registry: every scalar field a
commit's `entity_properties` may write, with its declared `value_type`
(`bool`/`i64`/`f64`/`date_time`/`keyword`/`text`/`bytes`) and advisory
`required` flag. Properties are graph-global, not per-type, so
`entity_type_defs[*].properties` is empty — this is the one place to read
"what fields exist and what type is each," the registry a faithful
write→read→rewrite (e.g. a replace-mode migration) needs.

relation_defs.description: Full relation definitions (domain/range, cardinality, inverse, flags).

term_count.description: Count of surface terms (labels/synonyms) in the semantic layer.

PlannerKeyHistograms.description: The per-(predicate, subject) and per-(predicate, object) count histograms.

bytes.description: Compressed chunk bytes of both artifacts, base and layers.

layer_bytes.description: Compressed chunk bytes the layers alone occupy.

layers.description: Delta layers over both artifacts, not yet folded into their bases.

PlannerPredicateStats.description: Exact visible counts for one predicate.

PlannerServingDefaults.description:
Adapter serving default derived from a promoted adapter run (today only
`extractor`): the LoRA adapter (a path on the model-serving volume) the
resident model loads per generate call.

adapter.description: Adapter path on the serving volume (the run manifest's artifact key).

run.description: The promoted registry run this adapter came from.

PlannerStatsResponse.description:
The statistics the SPARQL planner reads for the published generation a
latest read uses (`GET /v1/graph/planner-stats`). Read from the
generation's manifest and sidecar metadata; never a scan of the graph.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page. A cursor
belongs to this generation: after a newer one is published it is
refused with `400` (`planner-stats cursor expired`), and paging starts
again without a cursor.

predicate_count.description: Predicates in the generation, across all pages.

predicates.description: One page of predicates, by triple count descending, then IRI.

published_at.description:
When the generation was published (RFC 3339, UTC). `null` while the
published manifest records no wall-clock time: its `created_at_micros`
only orders generations.

oneOf.description:
The generation's commit watermark; `null` when the graph has no
published generation.

value_order_index.description:
Value-order index coverage: the plan `GET /v1/graph/index-upgrade`
reports.

predicates_covered.description:
Label predicates in this generation that the sidecar serves. Empty
