unless every PSO table carries a sidecar.

PlattCalibration.description:
Inline Platt calibration `(a, b)`: maps a raw retrieval score `s` to
`P(relevant) = 1/(1 + exp(a·s + b))`. The server pins it to the snapshot it
serves, so the emitted confidence is reproducible per snapshot
(FAL-DERIVED-DETERMINISM). Fit offline with `lbb-retrieval`'s `PlattScaler`.

PropertiesInput.description:
The accepted shapes of [`EntityPropertiesInput::properties`]: a list of
[`PropertyInput`] objects, or a flat map of field name to
[`FlatPropertyValue`].

PropertyInput.description: One literal property: an ontology field name plus a typed value.

PropertyMergeMode.description:
Whether an `entity_properties` write merges with or replaces the entity's
already-stored fields. See [`TripletCommitFile::property_merge`]. The default
is `Merge`: an entity's attributes accumulate across commits, the
least-surprising semantics for incremental enrichment. `Replace` is the
deliberate, destructive mode for re-stating or pruning an entity's full set.

PropertyValueInput.description:
A typed literal value for ingest. The variant must match the field's declared
`PropertyType`; `date_time` is an ISO-8601 string stored as microseconds.

oneOf.description:
Members of a `keyword_set` field. Order and duplicates don't matter on
the wire; the commit path canonicalizes (sorts, deduplicates) at rest.

keyword_set.description:
Members of a `keyword_set` field. Order and duplicates don't matter on
the wire; the commit path canonicalizes (sorts, deduplicates) at rest.

oneOf.description: Members of an `i64_set` field; canonicalized like `keyword_set`.

i64_set.description: Members of an `i64_set` field; canonicalized like `keyword_set`.

PublicationState.description: Server-managed publication lifecycle for one graph epoch.

PublicationStatusResponse.description:
One bounded status document for automatic exact-generation publication.
It is available before the first generation publishes, unlike
[`PublishedReadStatusResponse`], so SDKs can wait without probing SPARQL.

PublishedGenerationEnqueueDisposition.description:
Whether an import's deterministic published-generation job was newly
queued or coalesced with equivalent pending work.

PublishedReadConformanceView.description:
Published conformance provenance. `validated_at_seq` may trail the common
query watermark while the next durable validation is running.

PublishedReadFamilyView.description:
One family present in an atomic published root. Object keys and ETags stay
internal; this is the bounded operational/API projection.

oneOf.description:
The watermark this family itself is served at. Absent on a
common-watermark root, where every family serves the root's
`served_at_seq`; present, and possibly lower, once a root records
per-family watermarks. Optional rather than defaulted: a missing value
must never decode as "carried at sequence 0".

PublishedReadSnapshotView.description:
Bounded introspection view of an immutable published generation. It exposes
snapshot lineage and freshness without leaking object-store keys.

oneOf.description:
The fail-closed visibility floor of this root: the minimum watermark
over every family. Absent on a common-watermark root, where it is
`served_at_seq` by construction. Optional rather than defaulted: a
missing value must never decode as a floor of sequence 0.

PublishedReadStatusResponse.description:
One coherent operational view of the graph head and the immutable read root
pinned while resolving it. Lag values are derived from this `head_seq`, not
from a separately-polled status response.

base_current.description:
True when the served base reflects the head: no commit lag and no
same-sequence ontology, shapes, or index-configuration change pending.

citations.description:
IRIs of the entities the answer names, at most 20. Each one appeared
in the rows the loop read; the server removes any other.

text.description: A short answer in plain words.

QueryAnswerStep.description: One tool call of the answer loop.

input.description: The model's input to the tool, a JSON object; long texts are cut.

ok.description: The tool answered; `false` when it failed (the model read the error).

rows.description:
Rows a `sparql` step returned; for a `compare` step, the entries that
differ (added, removed and changed).

QueryAnswerStepEvent.description: One tool call of a streamed answer loop ended.

input.description: What the tool was asked, in one line of at most 200 characters.

QueryAnswerTool.description: A tool the answer loop can call.

QueryCompareChange.description: One key whose rows differ between the two points.

after.description: Its rows at the later point, without the key; at most 20.

before.description: Its rows at the earlier point, without the key; at most 20.

QueryComparePoint.description: One point of a comparison: exactly one of a commit, a date, or a moment.

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`: the last commit written by the end of that day, UTC.

moment.description: RFC 3339: the last commit written at or before it.

QueryComparePointResult.description: Where one point of a comparison read, and how much.

as_of_commit_seq.description: The commit read; absent only when the latest read named none.

committed_at.description: When the commit was written, RFC 3339, when the server knows it.

total.description: Rows the query has at this point.

QueryCompareRequest.description:
Run one `SELECT` at two points and pair the rows
(`POST /v1/query/compare`).

oneOf.description: The later point; default the latest commit.

cursor.description:
`next_cursor` of the page before, with the same request otherwise.
It pins both commits.

key.description:
Variables that identify a row's entity, at most 8 (for example
`["contact"]`). With a key the server pairs the rows by it: `added`
and `removed` hold the rows of keys at one point only, and `changed`
the keys whose rows differ. Without a key whole rows are compared.

limit.description: Entries of each list per page: 1 to 1,000, default 100.

max_rows.description:
Rows the server reads per point: 1 to 50,000, default 20,000. Past
it the comparison is `truncated`.

query.description:
A SPARQL `SELECT`, at most 20,000 characters. Leave out `LIMIT`: the
server pages through the rows itself.

QueryCompareResolution.description: How a point of a comparison was found.

QueryCompareResponse.description: The rows that differ between two points of one query.

key.description: The key the rows were paired by; empty when whole rows were compared.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor`, with the same request, for the next page.

notes.description: What to know about the result: a cut, blank nodes, a `LIMIT`.

offset.description: The index of the first entry of this page in each list.

truncated.description:
A point was not read whole (`max_rows`, or the time ran out), so the
difference is not complete.

QueryCompareTotals.description: The size of each list of a comparison, over all pages.

added.description:
Rows of the later point that the earlier one has not (of keys only at
the later point, with a key).

changed.description: Keys whose rows differ; 0 without a key.

removed.description: Rows of the earlier point that the later one has not.

unchanged.description: Keys (or rows, without a key) that are the same at both points.

properties.description:
The properties its sampled instances use, the most used first, with
their coverage. Empty when the class was not sampled yet.

values.description:
A small class (at most 30 instances): its instances with their label
and literal values. Absent for a larger class, or when the background
sample has not read it yet (`partial`).

QueryDescribeCoverage.description: How many sampled instances of a class hold one property.

example.description: A short example value (a literal, with its datatype).

instances.description: Sampled instances that have the property.

of.description:
Instances sampled: the class's instances, at most 100. A filter on a
property that few instances hold returns few rows.

target.description: The class of the linked entities, when the values are entities.

QueryDescribeInstance.description: One instance of a small class, with its label and literal values.

values.description: Property IRI → its literal value (the first one), as written.

links.description: `true` when its values are entities, `false` for literal values.

statements.description: Statements in the graph, from the schema summary.

used_by.description: The classes whose sample has it, the most instances first; at most 3.

QueryDescribeRequest.description:
Describe the parts of the graph a question needs
(`POST /v1/query/describe`). With neither `question`, `classes` nor
`properties`, the largest described classes.

classes.description: Class IRIs to describe, at most 20.

properties.description: Property IRIs to describe, at most 50.

question.description:
A question: the classes and properties whose names, labels or
comments match its words. At most 4,000 characters.

QueryDescribeResponse.description: The parts of the graph a question needs, as JSON and as compact text.

age_ms.description: Milliseconds since the server built the description it read.

commit_seq.description: The commit of the published generation the description was read from.

partial.description:
The background sample has not read every class yet: coverage and the
values of small classes can be missing. Ask again in a minute.

prefixes.description: `PREFIX` name → namespace, for the names `text` uses.

text.description: The same description as compact text, for a model's prompt.

unknown.description: IRIs of the request that the graph has no class or property for.

QueryDescribeStatement.description: One OWL or RDFS statement about a described class or property.

object.description: An IRI, or a literal's text.

QueryDescribeUse.description:
One class that uses a property, and how many of its sampled instances
hold it.

QueryHistoryResolution.description: How the loop found the commit of a `history` answer.

QueryLinkMethod.description: How a name of the question matched the name of an entity.

QueryNamesRequest.description:
Find the entities a question or a list of names names
(`POST /v1/query/names`).

text.description: A question, or names: 1 to 4,000 characters.

QueryNamesResponse.description: The names of a text and the entities each may mean.

candidates.description:
Each candidate of each name found, in the order of the text; the
candidates of one name share its `text`, the one to prefer first.
Empty when no name linked, or when the index was not ready.

commit_seq.description: The commit of the graph description the index was built from.

index_names.description: Names in the index the matching read.

index_ready.description:
The graph's name index was ready. When `false` the server builds it
in the background: ask again in a few seconds.

QueryRewriteAnchor.description: What the server read about one anchored IRI.

found.description: The IRI has statements at the read commit.

note.description:
Why the IRI did not reach the rewriter as an entity: it is not in
the graph, or its read failed or ran out of time.

QueryRewriteEvent.description:
One event of a streamed question: `POST /v1/query/ask` with
`Accept: text/event-stream`. On the wire each event is
`event: <event>\ndata: <data as JSON>\n\n`. The order: `grounding`,
`route`, a `step` per tool call of the loop, `answer`, then `done`; a
second `route` comes before `answer` when the loop chose another route.
`mode: "route"` sends `grounding`, `route` and `done`. `error` ends a
stream that failed. Clients ignore an event name they do not know: later
versions add events.

QueryRewriteEventDone.description: The whole response: the same JSON as the response without a stream.

data.description: The whole response: the same JSON as the response without a stream.

QueryRewriteEventRoute.description:
The router's route as soon as it answers, the caller's route at once,
or the loop's route when it answers.

data.description:
The router's route as soon as it answers, the caller's route at once,
or the loop's route when it answers.

QueryRewriteEventStep.description: One tool call of the loop ended.

data.description: One tool call of the loop ended.

QueryRewriteExample.description:
One worked example of a profile: a question and the query that answers
it on this graph.

note.description: Why the query is written so; at most 1,000 characters.

question.description: The question as a person asks it; at most 1,000 characters.

sparql.description:
A SPARQL `SELECT` or `ASK` query with its `PREFIX` declarations; at
most 4,000 characters. The server parses it on write.

QueryRewriteGrounding.description: The graph description the models read.

age_ms.description:
Milliseconds since the server built it (it keeps one per graph for 10
minutes).

commit_seq.description: The commit of the published generation the description was read from.

focus_classes.description:
Classes in the part of the description written for this question:
the classes whose names match the question and that the rest of the
description leaves out or cuts short.

focus_properties.description: Properties in the part of the description written for this question.

names.description:
Names in the name index the linking read; absent when no index was
ready (the linking was skipped).

profile_version.description:
The version of the graph's stored profile (`PUT
/v1/query/rewrite/profile`) the model read; absent when the graph
has no profile, or an empty one.

text.description:
The description itself, when the request asked for it
(`include_grounding`): the part every question reads, then the part
for this question.

QueryRewriteGroundingEvent.description: The graph description is ready (the first event of a stream).

age_ms.description: Milliseconds since the server built the description.

cached.description: The node had the description in its cache.

QueryRewriteHistory.description:
Where a `history` answer read the graph: the commit of a date, or the
two points of a comparison and what differs between them.

added.description:
A comparison's rows that the later point has and the earlier one has
not; with a `key`, the rows of the entities only the later point has.
At most 500.

as_of_commit_seq.description: The commit the query read; for a comparison, the earlier point.

as_of_date.description:
The date the loop resolved (`YYYY-MM-DD`): of the query's commit, or
of a comparison's earlier point.

changed.description:
With a `key`: the entities whose rows differ, with their rows at both
points. At most 500.

compare.description:
The answer comes from the loop's `compare` tool: the query ran at the
earlier point and at the later one (`query.as_of_commit_seq`), and
the lists below hold what differs.

key.description:
The variables the rows of a comparison were paired by. Empty when
whole rows were compared.

label.description: The label of the timeline point the date resolved to.

removed.description:
A comparison's rows that the earlier point has and the later one has
not; with a `key`, the rows of the entities only the earlier point
has. At most 500.
Without a key a changed value shows as a removed row and an added row.

oneOf.description: How the loop found `as_of_commit_seq`.
The size of each list before the cut at 500.

truncated.description:
The difference is not complete: a run did not read all its rows, or
a list holds more than 500 entries (`totals` has their number).

QueryRewriteLink.description:
One name of the question that the server linked to an entity of the
graph. A name with several close candidates has up to three entries with
the same `text`, the best first; an app can show "Did you mean …?".

class.description: The class the entity's name was read under.

score.description: 0 to 1: how well the words match the name.

text.description: The words of the question, as written.

QueryRewriteModelCall.description: One model call of a question.

cost_micro_usd.description: Estimate, in millionths of a US dollar.

tokens.description: Input plus output tokens, cache reads and writes included.

dry_run.description:
A preview (`dry_run=true`): the profile a write would store, with the
version it would get. Nothing was stored.

updated_at.description: When this version was written (RFC 3339); absent for version 0.

version.description: 0 when the graph has no profile; each write adds 1.

QueryRewriteProfileRequest.description:
Store the graph's rewrite profile (`PUT /v1/query/rewrite/profile`):
notes and examples the model of `POST /v1/query/ask` reads for every
question of the graph.

examples.description: At most 20 worked examples, 32,000 characters together.

expected_version.description:
The version this write replaces: the `version` a read returned, 0
when the graph has no profile yet. When the stored version differs,
the write answers `409 conflict` and stores nothing. Without it, the
write replaces any version.

notes.description:
What the data means, which property holds the current state, what
"me" or "my" means: at most 8,000 characters.

QueryRewriteRequest.description:
Answer a question about the graph (`POST /v1/query/ask`). An unknown
field answers `400`: the one-shot rewrite's `run` and `previous` are gone.

anchor.description:
Entity IRIs the user picked in the app, at most 10. The server reads
each one at the read commit (its types, its label, and a summary of
its links) and tells the rewriter to use these IRIs directly instead
of matching their names. An IRI that is not in the graph gets a note
in `anchors`, not an error. `mode: "route"` reads no anchors.

as_of_commit_seq.description: Read the graph at this commit.

context.description:
The app's notes for the model: what the data means, units, names to
prefer. At most 8,000 characters. Keep it the same across questions,
so the model provider's prompt cache reads it. The graph's stored
profile (`PUT /v1/query/rewrite/profile`) is read as well.

include_grounding.description:
Return the graph description the models read in `grounding.text`:
to see why an answer came out as it did, or to reuse the description
in an app's own prompt.

limit.description: Rows each query of the loop returns: 1 to 1,000, default 100.

oneOf.description: Fix the route: the router model is not asked.

timeline.description:
Dated points that stand for the graph's commits, at most 200. The
loop's `commit_for_date` and `compare` read a date as the commit of
the latest point on or before it, instead of the commit written last
on or before the end of that day (UTC). For graphs whose commits
stand for other dates (a demo's milestones, an import of old
records).

today.description:
Today's date for relative questions ("last 14 days"), `YYYY-MM-DD`.
Default: the server's UTC date.

anchors.description:
What the server read about each anchored IRI (`anchor`), in the
request's order.

oneOf.description:
The answer in plain words with its citations. Absent for `mode:
"route"`, and when the loop stopped before it answered (`error` says
why); `query` and `result` then hold the best rows it read.

attempts.description: Queries the loop ran (its `sparql` and `compare` steps).

error.description: Why the loop stopped before it answered.

oneOf.description:
For a `history` answer, or one that comes from a comparison: where
the loop read the graph and what differs.

linked.description:
Names of the question linked to entities of the graph before the
loop started; the model uses their IRIs directly.

oneOf.description:
The query whose rows hold the answer: the step the answer names,
else the last query with rows. Absent for `mode: "route"`, and when
no query answers the question.

rationale.description:
One sentence: which rows answer the question, or why the loop
stopped. For `mode: "route"`, who chose the route.

oneOf.description:
The rows of `query`: the first rows, the search report, and the eval
`trace_id` (the question is the trace's request). Absent for a
comparison: `history` holds what differs.

steps.description: The tool calls of the loop, in order.

QueryRewriteTerm.description:
One value of a row of a comparison, as SPARQL 1.1 Query Results JSON
writes it.

QueryRewriteTimelinePoint.description:
One dated point of an app's own timeline: the commit that stands for a
date. For a graph whose commits stand for other dates than the days they
were written (a demo's milestones, an import of old records).

as_of_commit_seq.description: The commit that holds the graph as it was on that date.

label.description:
A name for the point ("Tender"), at most 200 characters. The
response's `history.label` repeats it.

QueryRewriteTimings.description: Where the time of a question went, in milliseconds.

anchor_ms.description: The reads of the anchored IRIs, beside the route.

link_ms.description:
The name linking, beside the route (the wait for a name index that
is not built yet included).

rewrite_ms.description: The rewriter model's turns of the loop.

QueryRoute.description: The kind of query a question needs.

QueryRouteDecision.description: The route of a question and how sure the choice is.

confidence.description:
0 to 1: the router's probability of `kind`, 1 for a route the caller
fixed, the rewriter's own estimate otherwise.

probabilities.description: The router's probability of each route, when the router answered.

RangedReadStats.description:
Read accounting for ranged (block-level) persisted index runs. Reported
when search served from a ranged layout instead of coarse whole objects.

attribute_blocks_fetched.description: Attribute blocks fetched to evaluate filter pruning.

block_bytes_fetched.description: Bytes fetched across all data and attribute blocks.

blocks_fetched.description:
Data blocks fetched with range reads (ANN cluster blocks; BM25
postings plus doc blocks).

blocks_skipped_by_attributes.description:
Blocks skipped thanks to attribute pruning (ANN clusters dropped from
the probe set; BM25 doc blocks never fetched).

candidates_pruned_by_attributes.description:
Candidate entries/postings dropped by attribute pruning before
scoring.

rerank_raw_bytes_fetched.description:
Bytes fetched from raw-f32 cluster regions to exactly rerank vector
candidates. Zero unless exact rerank was requested and the run carries
a raw region.

RdfSchemaObjectKind.description: The RDF node kind of a bounded observed-schema statement object.

RdfSchemaStatement.description: One OWL/RDFS vocabulary or annotation statement retained for schema UIs.

RdfSchemaSummaryResponse.description:
Compact, immutable observed-schema artifact attached to one exact F3 base.

This is the overview/read-model surface for Explorer and Ontology. It is
produced by maintenance while publishing F3 and is therefore cheap to read:
no request-time graph scan or base-plus-delta assembly is required.

literal_predicate_counts.description:
Per-predicate totals of literal-valued statements, the data-property
sibling of `resource_predicate_counts`. `None` when the stored summary
artifact predates this field; the next full summary rebuild fills it.

RdfSchemaTermCount.description:
One exact RDF term count in the compact observed-schema summary.

`term` is the complete IRI rather than a display-local name. This keeps
foreign vocabularies unambiguous; clients may choose their own prefix or
local-name presentation.

RegionAnchorInput.description:
A page-region provenance anchor on a fact's evidence (region provenance
§4.1/§6.4(b) BYO import): where the evidence appears in the source
document. Coordinates are **normalized to the page box** (`[0, 1]`, origin
top-left, y down) with `x0 <= x1` and `y0 <= y1`; `confidence` is the
extraction confidence in `[0, 1]`. The commit path validates and quantizes
(`round(v * 65535)` coords, `round(c * 255)` confidence) into the canonical
stored anchor; out-of-range, non-finite, or inverted boxes are rejected.

page.description: 0-based page index within the source document.

RelationAdjacencyCount.description:
Exact current-edge count for one observed source-type / relation /
target-type combination. The graph summary already scans the reduced edge
set, so exposing this rollup lets schema visualizations avoid one additional
whole-snapshot query per populated relation.

RemoveEntityTypeOp.description:
Tombstone an entity type: existing records of the type stay readable
(the def is retained, so they still resolve), but it is rejected for new
commits. Conflicts when current entities of the type exist; blocked until
those entities are migrated or retracted.

RemoveRelationOp.description:
Tombstone a relation: existing edges stay readable but it is rejected for
new commits. Conflicts when current edges use it; blocked until those
edges are migrated or retracted.

RenameEntityTypeOp.description:
Rename an entity type's display name. The frozen cross-version stable id
is unchanged, so every existing record keeps resolving (now to the new
name) and entity identity is preserved — only the display name and
future commits-by-name change. Errors if `to` already names a different
type. A no-op if the type is already named `to`.

RenameRelationOp.description:
Rename a relation's display name (stable id frozen; existing edges keep
resolving to the new name). Errors on a collision with a different
relation; a no-op if already named `to`.

ResolveTermRequest.description:
WS11 — snap-back resolve: map a piece of free text (a model's guess at a
class, relation, property, or value) to the nearest item that actually
exists in the graph's vocabulary. The output is a subset of real vocabulary
by construction — the resolver never fabricates a term.

candidates.description:
Restrict resolution to this explicit candidate set (the narrowed
shortlist — e.g. relations WS10 admitted for a type pair). Each candidate
is classified against the ontology for its `kind`. When absent the
resolver draws candidates from the graph's schema vocabulary.

kinds.description:
Which vocabulary sources to consider; empty means all. Ignored when
`candidates` is supplied (the candidate list is the search space).

text.description: The free text to snap to real vocabulary (1..=256 chars).

top_k.description: Max matches to return (default 3, clamped to 25).

method.description:
How the matches were ranked: `embedding` (the graph's managed model,
semantic) or `lexical` (trigram/edit-distance, the always-available
fallback used when no managed embedding is configured).

description.description:
Ontology description/definition when the resolved schema term carries
one. Candidate-free class resolution preserves tenant-authored class
documentation instead of returning only a bare label.

score.description: Similarity to the input in [0, 1]; higher is closer.

oneOf.description:
Structured schema signature for class, relation, and property
candidates. This is derived from the same pinned ontology as the
candidate and provenance.

RetractEdgeInput.description: One edge to retract, identified the same way it was asserted.

RetrievalProfileId.description:
Named retrieval profile selecting the fusion knobs (BM25 normalization,
channel weights, score floor, degree-boost mode, ontology class-intent +
expansion de-noise). A closed enum — the only profile identifier that may
reach a metric label — so the cardinality stays bounded.

- `ndcg_v1` is the **shipped default** (a search that names no profile
  resolves to it): `graph_aware_v1` plus candidate-scoped lexical scoring
  and a moderate vector lift, selected by the 2026-06-22 nDCG@10 gate.
- `graph_aware_v1` is the graph-aware comparison anchor: ontology class-intent
  surfacing + entity-fold expansion de-noise, ≈2.5× nDCG@10 over the legacy
  blend on membership/dimension queries, generalising cross-corpus with the
  same knobs and inert on graphs without ontology class structure
  (retrieval-quality-ledger R21/R23).
- `baseline` is the historical hardcoded blend — kept selectable as the
  comparison anchor and the instant rollback path.
- `scored_atom_v1` flips BM25 to the candidate-set-independent theoretical-max
  normalizer (`S_max`): quality-neutral on a single lexical channel, better
  cross-channel fusion calibration (retrieval-quality-ledger R15/R16).

RewrittenQuery.description: The query whose rows hold the answer.

as_of_commit_seq.description: The commit the query read; for a comparison, the later point.

entailment.description: The entailment the query needs; pass it to `POST /v1/query/sparql-text`.

sparql.description: A SPARQL `SELECT` or `ASK` query, with its `PREFIX` declarations.

RowPage.description:
Final-result row page metadata. `total` is the number of rows after filters,
projection/deduplication, grouping, and ordering but before the requested
response page is sliced. `returned` is the number of rows actually present in
this response page.

ontology_version.description: Ontology identity the durable report validated.

shapes_version.description: Shapes identity the durable report validated.

truncated.description:
True when `result_count` is exact but `results` contains only the
caller-requested leading window. Whole-graph audits can produce one row
per offending focus node, so HTTP responses are bounded by default.

oneOf.description:
Published conformance watermark. Present on every public durable
conformance response; absent only on internal pre-publication
validation results.

details.description:
Nested results explaining a composite violation (`sh:detail`), e.g.
which constraint inside a `sh:node` shape the value node failed.

source_node_shape.description:
The containing root/node shape that selected the focus node. This stays
actionable when `source_shape` is an inline `sh:property` blank node.

source_shape.description:
The exact SHACL shape that emitted the result. For inline property
constraints this may be a blank node.

oneOf.description:
Durable audit health summary recorded with the schema bundle, when one
has been published by background validation. The metadata-only
`/v1/schema` route does not run validation in the request path.

constraint_shape_count.description:
Internal SHACL shape count including referenced property/logical shapes.
Useful for debugging parser expansion without making `shape_count`
surprising to authors.

shape_count.description:
User-visible active shape count: root SHACL shapes that select focus
nodes, not the inline `sh:property` blank-node constraints.

shapes.description:
Every shape of the active set as the validator parsed it: the root
shapes that select focus nodes and the property, node, and logical
shapes they reference. Terms use the N-Triples form the conformance
report uses (`<iri>`, `_:label`, `"lexical"^^<datatype>`), so a report
result's `source_node_shape`, `source_shape`, and `result_path` match a
shape's `id` and `path` exactly. Empty when no shapes are active.

iri.description: Canonical query IRI minted by Little Big Brain for this class identity.

oneOf.description:
Absent until maintenance publishes conformance for this exact shapes
version. Schema publication never performs whole-graph validation in an
HTTP handler.
How and when the engine enforces the published shapes on this graph.

SchemaShapeConstraint.description: One constraint parameter of a shape.

parameter.description:
The SHACL parameter's local name: `minCount`, `class`, `datatype`,
`in`, `pattern`, `node`, `property`, `or`, `qualifiedValueShape`,
`sparql`, and so on.

values.description:
The parameter's values. Terms (a class, a datatype, a referenced
shape, an `sh:in` member) use N-Triples form; counts and lengths are
decimal numbers; `pattern` is the regular expression, `nodeKind` the
`sh:` local name, `languageIn` the tags, and `sparql` the SELECT text.

SchemaShapeTarget.description: How a root shape selects its focus nodes.

kind.description:
`class` (`sh:targetClass`, or the shape is itself a class), `node`
(`sh:targetNode`), `subjects_of` (`sh:targetSubjectsOf`), or
`objects_of` (`sh:targetObjectsOf`).

term.description: The class, node, or predicate term.

SchemaShapeView.description: One parsed SHACL shape: a node shape, or a property shape when `path` is set.

closed.description: `sh:closed true`: a focus node may carry only the declared properties.

constraints.description: The constraint parameters, in declaration order.

deactivated.description: `sh:deactivated true`: the validator skips the shape.

ignored_properties.description: `sh:ignoredProperties` of a closed shape, as `<iri>` terms.

message.description: The shape's `sh:message`, when it declares one.

path.description:
The property path in SPARQL path syntax (`

`, `^

`, `

/`), the form of the report's `result_path`. Absent for a node shape.

targets.description: How the shape selects focus nodes. Only root shapes have targets.

shape.description: An active root shape: one that selects focus nodes.

format.description:
Format hint for this source. Ontology sources use the ontology importer
formats (`auto`, `lbb_json`, `json_ld`, `rdf_xml`, `csv`, `tsv`, or
`spec`). SHACL shapes use RDF graph formats only: `auto`/`turtle`,
`n_triples`, `n_quads`, or `trig`.

SchemaWriteEnforcement.description: How the published shape set is enforced on this graph.

write_enforceable.description:
True when no root shape has a blocker. An RDF-native graph accepts
`reject` mode only for such a shape set.

SchemaWriteEnforcementBlocker.description:
A constraint with no bounded affected set: the engine cannot tell which
focus nodes a write changes its verdict for.

constraint.description:
The SHACL parameter: `sh:sparql`, or the shape reference that closes a
cycle (`sh:node`, `sh:property`, `sh:or`, ...).

shape.description: The shape that carries the constraint.

SchemaWriteEnforcementTiming.description: When the engine checks the published shapes against a write.

ScoredCandidateInput.description:
One scored retrieval candidate on the wire: which entity matched and its raw
(pre-calibration) score from whatever channel produced it. The entity is
referenced by selector (id, or type+name); a candidate not visible in the
served snapshot is dropped, not emitted (inv. candidate-not-final).

aliases.description:
Other names this entity is known by: when SAME_AS-linked entities fold
onto one canonical hit, the folded members' names (and record aliases)
surface here. Absent for entities with no SAME_AS component.

attributes.description:
Requested entity attributes, read from the same loaded snapshot used to
rank this hit. Absent when the request did not ask for a projection.

oneOf.description:
Auditable fusion accounting. Present only when `explain=true`; the
weighted channel contributions plus `post_fusion_adjustment` reproduce
`final_score` within floating-point tolerance.

SearchConditionResolved.description:
One filter condition as the search resolved it, in request order: the
classes of a class condition, or a relationship condition's IRI,
direction, and entities.

SearchConsistency.description:
Read consistency for a query surface (search, graph summary, SPARQL).

A5 (2026-07-21 product decision): `Eventual` is the **default**. It serves the
pinned published generation at its watermark with no request-time graph
assembly — the lowest-latency mode and the availability floor during any
publication backlog. The served watermark rides back on
`SnapshotView::served_at_seq`. `Strong` requires the immutable published
generation itself to cover the query head and is explicit opt-in; the precise
read-your-writes contract (`min_indexed_seq`) replaces most former uses of strong. See
`docs/architecture/segment-native-indexing.md` §6.

SearchDirection.description: Which way a relationship condition reads.

oneOf.description:
Co-bind the candidates with a graph anchor's neighborhood (the
engine-native query-conditional join; R17). `None` == no graph constraint.

A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq`. Take the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned, then read with `min_indexed_seq` set to it. Under the default
`Eventual` consistency, a floor not yet covered by published state returns a
retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429 (poll until it lands) rather than a
silently stale answer. Under `Strong` the floor is satisfied by construction
(strong covers head); a floor above head is a client error. `None` == no
floor. See `docs/architecture/segment-native-indexing.md` §6.
Named retrieval profile (fusion knobs). `None` == shipped default.

query_vector.description:
Client-computed query vector for the vector signal; when present the
provider only identifies the embedding space.

rerank.description:
Opt into exact raw-f32 reranking of the persisted vector candidates.
Only effective when the run carries a raw-f32 region (built with
`include_raw`); otherwise it is a no-op. Default off keeps the compact
4-bit-approximate path.

rerank_top_k.description:
How many top approximate candidates to re-score exactly before
truncating to the result `top_k`. Defaults to a small multiple of
`top_k` when unset; ignored unless `rerank` is set.

impressions_scanned.description:
Impression objects scanned to build `impressions` (0 unless the request
passed `?include=impressions`).

SearchFeedbackExportImpression.description:
One opt-in-logged search's ranking context, returned in the training export
under `?include=impressions`. The `split` mirrors the query family's labeled
split (or a deterministic hash split when the query has no labels yet), so
negatives mined from `shown` respect the same holdout as the labels.

embedding_model_id.description:
The embedding model in force when the search ran; keeps mined negatives in
the same embedding space as the labels (`None` for an unmanaged graph).

impressions.description:
Present only when the request passed `?include=impressions`. The raw
ranking context of opt-in-logged searches (L1), split-tagged consistently
with the labeled rows so a trainer can mine shown-but-unlabeled entities
as sampled negatives without straddling the train/eval holdout.

target_missing.description:
The judged target no longer exists at the source graph's head (deleted or
never committed). Trainers skip these; a UI can prompt relabeling. Only
computed when the export caller supplies a live-target resolver (the HTTP
endpoint and `lbb-testctl graph feedback-export` both do, from a loaded
snapshot that respects visibility); otherwise it stays `false`. Additive:
`serde(default)` false. Golden-pinned field name.

retracted.description:
A retraction of a prior label for this `(query, target, labeler)`. Sent as
a normal append (`POST /v1/search/feedback` with `retracted: true`) so the
audit trail is preserved — nothing is deleted. The export drops the tuple
when the *latest* event for it is a retraction; a later non-retracted
resubmission revives it. Additive: `serde(default)` false keeps every
pre-retraction stored label decodable. Golden-pinned field name.

untrainable_labels.description:
Accepted labels that cannot currently produce a training-export row.
This is an explicit warning signal: the append-only audit event is kept,
but a trainer will exclude it until that target kind is supported.

SearchFeedbackSummaryResponse.description:
Constant-size administration view over the feedback ledger. Unlike the
qrels export this never returns label or impression rows.

latest_label_sequence.description:
Append-only event count for polling. Exact unless `truncated` is true;
idempotent replays do not advance it and retractions do.

objects_scanned.description:
Label objects fetched for this request. Zero on a materialized-cache hit;
a rebuild reports the bounded source objects it read.

SearchFilter.description:
One condition of a search's filter: a class (`class`), or a relationship
to entities (`via`, `to`, and optionally `direction`).

oneOf.description:
Keep the instances of these classes (one IRI or a list, any of) and
of their subclasses. An embedding on a class above one takes part,
with only these classes' instances.

`out` (default): the hit links to the entity; `in`: the entity links
to the hit.

The entities (any of): IRIs, or names matched against the labels of
the entities `via` reaches (exact, then case and separators ignored,
then one clearly closest label).

via.description:
The relationship: a local name the instances use (`calls`), a known
prefix (`schema:knows`), or a full IRI (`<https://…>`).

oneOf.description:
Set membership: matches when the field has **any** member equal to one of
`values`. On a scalar field this behaves like `in`. The natural
authorization filter: `{"op":"overlaps","field":"acl","values":[…]}`
admits a document whose ACL set intersects the caller's principals.
`contains_any` is accepted as an alias.

Set membership: matches when the field has a member equal to **every**
one of `values`. On a scalar field this only matches a single-element
`values` equal to the scalar.

Negated `overlaps`: matches when the field has **no** member equal to any
of `values` — including when the field is absent.

SearchFilterReport.description:
A search's filter: its conditions as resolved and, with a relationship
condition, how it ran and how many entities it allows.

allowed.description:
Entities of the searched classes that meet every condition. In mode
`after` it is the selective limit plus one (there are more).

class.description: The class of the embedding that found the hit.

embedding.description: The embedding that found the hit.

id.description: The RDF term id of the IRI (hex).

relevance.description:
With a rerank: the model's probability (0 to 1) that the hit answers
the search text. The hits are ordered by it; `score` stays the
similarity.

post_fusion_adjustment.description:
Type boosts, score floors/clamps, graph-anchor boosts, observation-owner
promotion, and class-intent promotion are accounted for here.

SearchOrder.description:
Sort direction for a query's `order_by` key. `Desc` is the default for the
implicit relevance ordering (highest score first); `Asc` is most useful when
ordering by a metadata field.

SearchOrderBy.description:
Deterministic ordering key for a search result page. The default (`Score`)
ranks by relevance; `Metadata` orders by a result's metadata field so a
client can page by, e.g., a timestamp or title. Either way ties break on the
stable document id, so paging with `offset` never skips or repeats a result.

oneOf.description: Order by relevance score (the default ranking).

Order by a string-valued metadata field. Results missing the field sort
last regardless of direction, then fall back to the document-id
tiebreaker, so the page boundary stays deterministic.

embedding.description:
Search one embedding by name. Without it, the search covers every
searchable class of the graph.

explain.description:
Plan the search without running it: the scope, the resolved filters,
and how the filter would run. No model call, no hits.

filter.description:
The conditions every hit must meet, checked in the graph at the
search's snapshot: `{"class": …}` keeps the instances of a class (one
IRI or a list, any of; their subclasses too; one class condition per
search), and `{"via": …, "to": …, "direction": …}` keeps the hits
linked to entities.

probe.description:
Clusters to read across the big runs (default 4·√clusters, at least
8). Runs of up to 4,096 entries are always read whole.

request.description:
The user's words behind this search. When present the server records
an eval trace and returns its `trace_id`.

rerank.description:
Order the best hits by how well each answers `text`, with the
managed rerank model (`true`), or keep the similarity order
(`false`). Without it the graph's search setting decides
(`GET /v1/search/settings`).

text.description: The query text; embedded with the serving version's model.

SearchRerankModel.description: A rerank model: who serves it and its id.

SearchRerankReport.description: The rerank of one search. Absent when the search did not rerank.

cached.description: Answers kept from an earlier search of the same text (no model call).

candidates.description:
Hits the model read: the best `2·top_k` that passed the graph check,
at least 20 and at most 40, or the graph's `rerank_depth`.

error.description: Why the rerank failed, in short.

moved.description: Hits that moved from their similarity rank.

SearchRerankSource.description: Why a search reranked: the graph's setting or the request's `rerank`.

SearchRerankStatus.description: What became of the rerank of one search.

dropped_by_graph.description: Candidates the graph check removed (deleted or re-typed entities).

oneOf.description: The oldest commit the searched embeddings have embedded through.

embeddings.description: The embeddings the search read, and how current each is.

explain.description: Only planned (`explain`): no hits and no model call.

oneOf.description: The relationship filter, as resolved and run.

hits.description:
The best hits over every searched embedding, by score; an entity two
embeddings hold comes back once, with its best score.

lag_commits.description:
The most published commits one searched embedding does not cover yet
(`served_at_seq` − its watermark); the embed job catches up by itself.

not_ready.description:
Embeddings in scope that are still building their first version; the
search skipped them.

oneOf.description:
The rerank, when the search reranked (the request or the graph's
setting asked for it).
The RDF snapshot every hit was checked against.

SearchSettings.description: The search settings of a graph (`GET /v1/search/settings`).

blend.description:
How a reranked search orders its candidates, 0 to 1: by
`blend·relevance + (1 − blend)·similarity`, the similarity scaled to 0
to 1 over the reranked candidates (min–max). Absent or 1: the rerank
model's order; 0: the similarity order.

probe_factor.description:
Clusters a search reads across the big runs, as a factor of the
default (`4·√clusters`, at least 8), 1 to 4. A request's `probe`
wins. Absent: the default.

rerank.description:
Every search of the graph orders its best hits with the rerank model,
unless a request sets `rerank`.

rerank_available.description:
The server has a rerank model. Without one a search keeps the
similarity order and reports `rerank.status: unavailable`.

rerank_depth.description:
Candidates the rerank model reads, 20 to 80. Absent: `2·top_k`, at
least 20 and at most 40.

oneOf.description: The managed rerank model (the catalog's `reranker` role).

SearchSettingsRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/search/settings`: change some of the graph's search settings.
A field left out keeps its value; `null` sets it back to its default.
Unknown fields are refused.

blend.description:
`blend·relevance + (1 − blend)·similarity`, 0 to 1; `null`: the
default (the rerank order).

probe_factor.description:
Clusters read, as a factor of the default, 1 to 4; `null`: the
default.

rerank.description: Turn the rerank on or off for every search of the graph.

rerank_depth.description: Candidates the rerank model reads, 20 to 80; `null`: the default.

type_boosts.description:
Optional per-entity-type multiplicative rank boost, keyed by entity type
name (e.g. `{"CHUNK": 1.5, "OntologyProposal": 0.0}`). A type absent from
the map is unaffected (multiplier 1.0); `0.0` soft-excludes a type. This
makes heterogeneous-type ranking type-aware — e.g. float document chunks
above ontology-meta entities — without a hard type filter.

SearchSuggestRequest.description:
Turn-level grounding: complete a prefix from the index's own vocabulary
(BM25 term dictionary, attribute directory) and the graph ontology
(classes, relations, properties). Never reads doc/postings blocks; the
completions are strings that provably exist in the graph at this snapshot.

oneOf.description:
Type-signature narrowing context. When either endpoint type is set,
`relation` suggestions are filtered and ranked by the graph's empirical
type signatures (the map `relation → {(src_type, dst_type)}` learned from
current edges at this snapshot), falling back to declared domain/range
only when it is narrower. A type pair with no history returns the
unfiltered ranking — narrowing never produces an empty relation set.

field.description: Restrict `attribute_value` suggestions to one attribute field.

kinds.description: Which suggestion sources to draw from; empty means all.

limit.description: Max suggestions to return (default 8, clamped to 50).

oneOf.description:
Explicit ranker-weight override. Precedence per field:
request > trained serving defaults (a promoted `suggest_ranker` run) >
the shipped kind weights. Mirrors `SearchSignalWeights` on search.

snapshot_token.description:
Opaque vocabulary token binding graph epoch, commit, and ontology
version. Feed it to a subsequent suggest/resolve request to fail closed
on vocabulary drift.

trained_ranker_run.description:
The promoted `suggest_ranker` run whose trained weights ranked this
response; absent when the shipped defaults (or a request override)
applied.

truncated.description: True when more candidates matched than `limit` returned.

document_frequency.description: Document frequency, when the source carries it (`term`).

signature_forced.description:
True when this is a `relation` suggestion and the request's type-signature
context (`src_type`/`dst_type`) admits exactly one relation — i.e. the type
pair *forces* this predicate. Only ever set under
[`SearchSuggestRequest::context`]; absent (via `skip_serializing_if`)
otherwise, so context-free responses are byte-identical to before WS10.

SearchTargetMatch.description: How a `to` value matched an entity.

SearchTargetResolved.description: A `to` value and the entity it resolved to.

SearchTargets.description: One entity or several, each an IRI or a name (a label).

SearchTemporalCoverage.description:
Provenance for the immutable family roots selected from one pinned published
generation. `ceiling_commit_seq` is that generation's common query
watermark; per-leg fields are `None` only when the corresponding leg was
disabled.

oneOf.description: Highest commit covered by the selected immutable BM25 root.

Base snapshot commit sequence of the selected BM25 run, or `None` when
the BM25 leg was disabled.

ceiling_commit_seq.description: Common query watermark of the pinned published generation.

oneOf.description: Highest commit covered by the selected immutable ANN root.

Base snapshot commit sequence of the selected ANN run, or `None` when
the vector leg was disabled.

SearchTimings.description: Where the time of a search went, in milliseconds.

check_ms.description: The graph check of the candidates.

filter_ms.description: Resolving a relationship filter and finding its allowed entities.

index_ms.description: Probing the runs and scoring their codes.

relevance_ms.description: Asking the rerank model how well each candidate answers the text.

rerank_ms.description: Reading the exact vectors of the best candidates and scoring them.

resolve_ms.description: Reading the embedding, its manifest, and its runs.

SearchTuningRound.description: The judge's notes of one round.

SearchTuningSettings.description: The search settings a tuning session changes.

probe_factor.description: Clusters read, as a factor of the default, 1 to 4.

rerank_depth.description: Candidates the rerank model reads, 20 to 80.

SearchTuningTest.description: The best variant against the baseline on the test queries.

SearchTuningVariant.description: One set of settings a session ran.

building_version.description: A newer version that builds while this one serves (a changed recipe).

oneOf.description: The commit its serving version has embedded through.

hits.description: The hits of this response it found.

query.description:
The natural-language query. The only required field — every other field
has a sensible default, so `{"query":"…"}` is a complete request.

targets.description:
Which result surfaces to return. Omitted or empty means the full default
set (concepts, entities, assertions, paths, observations) rather than a
rejected request — a caller no longer has to guess this field.

suggested_queries.description:
Populated only when the result set is empty: index-grounded
alternatives (vocabulary terms, schema labels) the caller might have
meant. Absent (not `[]`) when there are results or rescue is disabled.

engine_remainder_ms.description:
Difference between `total_ms` and the sum of the named engine phases.
This captures response assembly and other small engine work that is not
worth a dedicated phase row.

oneOf.description:
Graph co-bind (`graph_anchor`) accounting. `mode` is set when a co-bind
ran; `anchor_resolved` is false if the anchor entity wasn't found (the
co-bind is then a no-op); `community_size` is the anchor neighborhood size.

published_lag_commits.description: Commit distance from the graph head to the pinned published generation.

oneOf.description:
The effective retrieval profile this search ran under (after the server
folds request > per-stack > server-default precedence into the request).
`None` == `baseline`. Lets a client (e.g. the console A/B view) label which
profile produced a result set.

target_prep_ms.description:
Time spent preparing the concrete search target set, optional filtered
target allow-list, and snapshot-visible target join set before BM25/vector
candidate generation.

oneOf.description:
Which persisted runs served this search relative to the resolved `as_of`
ceiling (BM25 and vector legs). Present only when `explain` is set. See
[`SearchTemporalCoverage`].

trained_fusion_run.description:
The promoted `fusion` model run whose trained weights served as this
search's channel-weight defaults (WS9 trainer loop). `None` when the
graph has no promoted fusion run or the request pinned an explicit
profile — so a client can label a ranking "trained (run N)" vs
"profile defaults" honestly.

vector_model_id.description:
The embedding model the vector leg actually searched: `Some(model_id)` for
a real-embedding space (a graph's managed `Stored` model or client-supplied
`ExternalVectors`), `None` for the char-trigram hash space (or when the
vector leg was disabled). Lets a client label the vector row honestly —
"real embeddings · {model}" vs "auto-derived from text (hash)".

SetPropertyConstraintOp.description:
Set (or clear) the enforced allowed-value set on an **existing** property
field — the tightening path for a field already in use (e.g. constrain
`status` to its ADR vocabulary). A non-empty list installs the `sh:in`
constraint that future commits are checked against; an empty list clears
it. Enforcement is write-time only: values already stored are not
retroactively validated. Errors on an unknown field or a non-enumerable
type. Bumps the ontology version.

allowed_values.description: Canonical allowed values; empty clears the constraint.

property.description: Name of the existing property field to constrain.

SetRelationCardinalityOp.description:
Change a relation's cardinality (`one_to_one` | `one_to_many` |
`many_to_one` | `many_to_many`). A narrowing transition is checked
against the exact current reduced edge projection before publication.
Once accepted, the declared cardinality is enforced on future commits.

SetRelationInverseOp.description:
Set (or replace) a relation's inverse-relation display name, enabling
one-hop reverse lookup (e.g. `PHASE_OF` for `HAS_PHASE`). Metadata
only — never touches stored edges.

hit_rate_at_k.description: Fraction of labeled queries whose expected entity appeared in top-k.

mrr_at_k.description: Mean reciprocal rank of the first expected target in top-k.

recall_at_k.description: Mean fraction of each query's expected targets recovered in top-k.

ShadowEvalRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/shadow-eval` — champion vs challenger retrieval over the
same pinned snapshot: the challenger is a search configuration (a
challenger embedding run's space, different weights, a profile), replayed
against the same queries the champion serves. Promotion stays a decision
on this evidence — the endpoint never promotes.

oneOf.description: Champion arm search options; `None` = the graph's serving defaults.

gate.description:
Fail-closed promotion verdict over the same labeled queries and pinned
snapshot. Requires quality non-regression plus p50/p95/p99 latency
ratios within the configured ceiling; this endpoint still never
performs the promotion itself.

labeled.description: Labeled queries (those with `expected`) the hit rates are over.

ShadowQuery.description:
One shadow-eval probe: a query and (optionally) the entity names that
count as a hit. Pairs come from captured signals, hand-written evals, or
the execution-verified synthetic generator.

overlap_at_k.description: |champion ∩ challenger| / k over the returned top-k names.

SignalEnvelope.description:
The stored form, one JSON object per NDJSON line. **[PIN]** the field set
(`v`, `kind`, `ts`, `request_id`, `snapshot_token`, `payload`) — Wave-5
consumers decode it.

ts.description: RFC 3339 capture timestamp, stamped by the server.

accepted.description: Number of signals written (0 when the feature flag is off).

object_key.description: The object the batch was flushed to, absent when nothing was written.

SignalInput.description:
One signal as a client sends it. The server stamps `v`, `ts`, and (when the
client omits it) `snapshot_token` to produce the stored [`SignalEnvelope`].

SignalKind.description:
The closed set of signal kinds (v1). Extending this is a deliberate format
change, not an open string.

v1.1 (2026-07-07, planner-feedback capture): adds the legacy
`ask_trace`/`ask_feedback` supervision records. They remain decodable for
durable training data, but no public Ask endpoint emits them.

`branch_merge_accepted`/`branch_merge_rejected` stay decodable for stored
signal records only: graphs have no branches, and nothing emits them.

SignalReadResponse.description:
`GET /v1/signals?from=&to=&limit=` — the consumer side of the signal bus:
signals whose flush seq lies in `[from, to]`, oldest first. Trainers split
on a pinned seq T (train ≤ T, eval > T) and record the window in the WS9
manifest's `data_lineage`.

objects_read.description: Objects fetched to serve this read (cost transparency).

truncated.description: True when the limit cut the result short.

SignatureSparsity.description:
How constrained the graph's relation type-signatures are. Sparse signatures
(many type pairs admitting exactly one relation) mean type-context alone
forces the predicate — the strongest, cheapest grounding.

forced_pct.description:
Fraction of observed (src_type, dst_type) pairs that admit exactly one
relation.

le3_pct.description: Fraction of observed type pairs that admit at most three relations.

type_pairs.description: Distinct type pairs observed in the current edge projection.

oneOf.description:
When a read was pinned with `as_of_commit_seq`, the pin that was applied.
This makes a pinned response self-describing — `commit_seq` still reports
the loaded head, so a caller can see both "you asked for N" and "head is
at M" instead of silently getting head.

compacted_seq.description:
Highest durable graph-truth commit folded by background compaction.
This is maintenance provenance, not the query-serving watermark.
Published reads expose their one common `served_at_seq` through the
response and `/v1/graph/read-snapshot`; handlers never fold the WAL tail
or assemble derived indexes to satisfy a request.

oneOf.description:
The coherent watermark named by the one immutable published generation
pinned for this response. All enabled families (RDF, Base, BM25, ANN,
summary, and conformance) are interpreted against this same
watermark; request pressure cannot select an older family or change it
mid-request. Omitted only for responses that do not use published state.

stale.description:
F2 (roadmap 18.3): true when this snapshot was served from the in-memory
cache while storage was degraded and the latest head could not be
verified — so `commit_seq` may not be the current head. Absent (false) on
every normal read; writes never serve stale. Omitted from the wire form
when false so healthy responses are byte-identical to before.

stale_reason.description:
The reason a read is `stale`. `"storage_degraded"` (F2),
`"eventual_consistency"` (served from the immutable published
generation); omitted when not stale.

SparqlAggregate.description:
One aggregate projection: `func(operand) AS as_var`. `operand` is absent for
`COUNT(*)` (count rows); for SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX it must resolve to a numeric
value (typically a `property` term). `distinct` applies to COUNT.

SparqlAggregateFunc.description: An aggregate function for a grouped SELECT.

SparqlCompareOp.description: A comparison operator for a SPARQL FILTER.

SparqlEntailment.description:
Entailment regime applied to a conformant SPARQL query. The regime is
evaluated at query time as a closure-driven pattern rewrite over the
dataset's asserted schema triples; the published dataset itself stays
asserted-only.

SparqlFilter.description:
A FILTER over a solution: a comparison, or a boolean composition of filters.
A comparison whose operands are unbound, incomparable, or a type mismatch is
not satisfied (treated as false).

SparqlGroup.description:
One result group of a grouped/aggregated SELECT: the GROUP BY key entities
(`keys`, identity keys) and typed scalar keys (`value_keys`, property /
date-bucket keys), plus each aggregate's value bound to its `as` variable.

keys.description: Entity-identity GROUP BY keys, under their variable name.

value_keys.description:
Typed scalar GROUP BY keys (from `group_keys` property/date-bucket
entries), each under its `as` name. Empty for a purely entity-keyed group.

SparqlGroupKey.description:
A GROUP BY key. `var` groups by the identity of the entity bound to a
variable (the legacy `group_by` behavior); `property` groups by a typed
scalar `field` read off that entity, projected into each group's
`value_keys` under `as`. Externally tagged
(`{"var": {…}}`, `{"property": {…}}`).

oneOf.description:
Group by the entity bound to `var` (identity). The group's `keys` map
carries the key entity under `var`, exactly like a `group_by` entry.

var.description:
Group by the entity bound to `var` (identity). The group's `keys` map
carries the key entity under `var`, exactly like a `group_by` entry.

oneOf.description:
Group by the typed scalar property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.
The value lands in each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Rows whose entity
lacks the property form a single `null`-valued group.

property.description:
Group by the typed scalar property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.
The value lands in each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Rows whose entity
lacks the property form a single `null`-valued group.

oneOf.description:
Group by a calendar truncation of a **datetime** property `field` of the
entity bound to `var` — the unit for a time series (commits per month,
events per day). The bucket label (e.g. `2026-06`, `2026-06-25`) lands in
each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Errors if `field` is not a datetime
property. Rows whose entity lacks the property form a `null`-valued group.

date_bucket.description:
Group by a calendar truncation of a **datetime** property `field` of the
entity bound to `var` — the unit for a time series (commits per month,
events per day). The bucket label (e.g. `2026-06`, `2026-06-25`) lands in
each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Errors if `field` is not a datetime
property. Rows whose entity lacks the property form a `null`-valued group.

SparqlKeyValue.description:
One typed GROUP BY key value projected into a group's `value_keys`: a typed
scalar (a property value, or a date-bucket label). Distinct from
[`SparqlScalar`] (numeric-only aggregate results) because a key can be a
string/keyword, datetime, or boolean. `null` is an unbound key (the entity
lacked the property).

oneOf.description: RFC3339 instant (a datetime property) or a bucket label (`2026-06`, etc.).

date_time.description: RFC3339 instant (a datetime property) or a bucket label (`2026-06`, etc.).

SparqlOrderBy.description:
One ORDER BY key. `var` names an aggregate `as` var or a GROUP BY key in
aggregated mode, or a bound variable otherwise; rows/groups are ordered by
that value (numeric for aggregates, entity name for entity keys).

SparqlProfileJoinOrder.description:
The order the planner chose for one basic graph pattern (`bgp`) or one
join group (`join_group`).

bound_before.description: Variables already bound when the order was chosen (a seeded join).

evaluations.description:
How many times the planner made this same decision in the request,
for example once per seed row.

steps_total.description: Steps in the decision; `steps` keeps at most 64.

SparqlProfileJoinStep.description: One step of a join order, in the order the planner chose.

estimate.description:
For `bgp`, the cardinality estimate the planner compared when it chose
this pattern, given the variables bound before it. For `join_group`,
the child's standalone estimate. Absent when not priced.

pattern.description:
The triple pattern (`bgp`) or a short label of the child group
(`join_group`). Literals are cut at 64 characters and the whole step
at 512, IRIs included; a cut ends with `…`.

rows_after.description: `join_group` only: the rows accumulated after this child folded in.

SparqlProfileJoins.description: Binary-join counters of a profiled request, by strategy.

SparqlProfileOperator.description:
One operator kind that ran in a profiled request. Counters an operator
does not keep are zero; its other counters are in `detail`.

SparqlProfilePlans.description: Which specialized plans ran, as counts of sub-plans.

histogram_runs.description: Grouped counts answered from the key histograms.

obj_window.description: Range FILTERs served from an object-value window.

pair_join_stats.description: Two-pattern join counts answered from the pair-count sidecar.

row_reuse.description: Join steps that reused their row buffers.

small_build.description: Hash joins that built on the smaller pattern side.

star_prefix.description: BGPs evaluated as a merged star plus the rest.

stats_answered.description: Sub-plans answered from index statistics, reading no data blocks.

str_byte.description: String tests evaluated on raw dictionary bytes.

summary_fast_path.description:
The published summary answered the query: `hit`, `entailed_hit`, or
`declined`. Absent on the structured route, which has no fast path.

typed_adjacency.description: Typed-adjacency grouped counts answered by the batched plan.

SparqlProfileReads.description: Object reads of a profiled request.

blocks.description: Block and dictionary reads the plan charged.

budget_trips.description: Times the request read budget stopped the query.

bytes_fetched.description:
Stored bytes of the block reads that missed the request block cache.
Such a read goes to the node's cache tiers (RAM, NVMe) or to object
storage, so a miss is not always an object-storage GET. Zero when the
request block cache is off.

cache_hits.description: Block reads the request block cache served; zero when it is off.

cache_misses.description: Block reads that missed the request block cache; zero when it is off.

peak_bytes_held.description: The request block cache's largest residency, in bytes.

SparqlProfileStage.description: One timed stage of a profiled request.

SparqlProfileWcoj.description: Worst-case-optimal join counters of a profiled request.

SparqlQueryProfile.description:
What the server measured while it answered one profiled SPARQL request.
It describes that request only. Times are milliseconds of wall time.

filter_type_errors.description:
FILTER conditions dropped by a type error (for example a comparison
between datatypes with no defined order).

join_orders.description:
The order the planner chose for each basic graph pattern and join
group, with its estimates. At most 64 records of 64 steps each.

join_orders_dropped.description: Distinct join orders past the 64-record bound.

operators.description: Operators that ran, with the rows they took and produced.

result_cache.description:
The result-cache outcome. Always `bypassed`: a profiled request never
reads or fills the cache.

stages.description:
Stage timings in order. The text route reports `resolve_snapshot`,
`parse_rewrite`, `execute` and `serialize`; the structured route
reports `resolve_snapshot`, `lower`, `execute` and `decode`.

total_ms.description: The whole request inside the graph store, snapshot resolution included.

trigram.description:
The label-trigram decision for a string FILTER: `used`, a decline
reason (`unsupported`, `no_sidecar`, `predicate_not_covered`,
`short_needle`, `or_chain`, `candidate_cap`, `not_selective`,
`live_delta`, `read_failed`), or absent when the query had no string
test the index could serve.

SparqlScalar.description:
A scalar aggregate result value. `null` is an empty AVG/MIN/MAX (no numeric
rows).

SparqlSearchEstimate.description:
The costs the planner compared when the entities that satisfy the rest
of the query fit under its limit, counted from cluster metadata. The
search-first plan runs when `search_first_entries` is below
`filter_first_scored`.

filter_first_entries.description:
Entries of the clusters that hold an allowed entity: what the
filter-first plan reads.

filter_first_scored.description: Allowed entities with a vector: what the filter-first plan scores.

search_first_allowed.description:
Allowed entities inside those nearest clusters: what the search-first
plan scores.

search_first_entries.description:
Entries of the nearest clusters the planner compared: the smallest
probe that holds enough allowed entities for the exact rerank, or the
first probe with at least `filter_first_scored` entries. What the
search-first plan reads.

SparqlSearchPlan.description: How the planner answered the search of one query.

SparqlSearchReport.description:
What the search inside a SPARQL query did. Its hits are bound into the
query as a `VALUES` block, so the rest of the query sees them as rows.

allowed.description:
Entities that satisfy the rest of the query, when the planner read
them; capped at 20,001.

complete.description:
False when fewer than `top` entities satisfy the query within the
candidates the search may score.

oneOf.description:
The oldest commit every searched embedding covers. Text changed after
it is searched with its earlier vector.

The costs behind the choice of plan, when `allowed` fit under the
planner's limit.

hits.description: The entities it found and bound.

lag_commits.description: Commits between the snapshot the query read and `embedded_through_seq`.

oneOf.description:
The rerank (`search:rerank true`), when the query asked for one and
the search had hits. The model read the best `2·top` hits (20 to 40)
and the best `top` by its relevance were bound; any other status
bound the `top` most similar, without a relevance.

rounds.description: Search rounds (a search-first plan widens until it has `top`).

top.description:
The entities the search was asked for: `search:top`, else the query's
`LIMIT` plus `OFFSET`, else 10.

usage.description: The model call for the query text, if one ran.

SparqlSearchTimings.description: The phases of one search inside a SPARQL query, in milliseconds.

check_ms.description: The graph checks of the candidates.

embed_ms.description: The query vector (0 when cached, given, or read from an entity).

filter_ms.description: The read of the entities that satisfy the rest of the query.

rerank_ms.description: The exact rescoring of the candidates.

resolve_ms.description: Embedding documents, manifests and class lists.

SparqlSelectRequest.description:
A SPARQL-subset SELECT/ASK query: a conjunctive basic graph pattern (the
WHERE) evaluated over the conformant published RDF dataset, with variable
projection, DISTINCT, and LIMIT/OFFSET. Structured-request-first — the SPARQL
text syntax is a later addition behind a dialect field, and FILTER plus
aggregation arrive in later milestones.

aggregates.description:
Aggregate projections (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX … AS …). Presence switches
the query into grouped/aggregated mode.

oneOf.description:
Exact transaction-time watermark from the retained graph-owned RDF
lineage. Uses the same bounded base and commit deltas as SPARQL text;
a missing checkpoint or a pin beyond head fails instead of serving a
different snapshot. Valid-time selectors are unsupported.

ask.description:
`ASK` form: return only `boolean` (whether the pattern has any solution).
Projection, DISTINCT, and limit/offset are ignored.

oneOf.description:
Read consistency. `eventual` (the default) pins the native RDF runset in
the current `PublishedReadSnapshot`; it never folds a gap or discovers
another family. The served watermark is surfaced as
`snapshot.served_at_seq`. A graph without a published generation returns
a retryable readiness error. `strong` requires that same immutable
generation to cover head and otherwise returns
`strong_read_pending`.

filters.description:
FILTER: boolean conditions on each solution, implicitly AND-ed. A solution
is kept only when every filter holds.

group_by.description:
GROUP BY: variables whose bound entities define the groups. When set (or
when `aggregates` is non-empty) the response returns `groups` instead of
`solutions`. Empty `group_by` with `aggregates` set yields one group over
the whole result.

group_keys.description:
GROUP BY keys richer than a bare entity variable: group by a typed scalar
`property` value (e.g. a commit's `area`), or a `date_bucket` truncation
of a datetime property (e.g. commits per month). Additive to `group_by`;
the effective grouping is the `group_by` variables (as entity-identity
keys) followed by these. Entity-identity keys land in each group's `keys`;
scalar keys land in `value_keys` under their `as` name. Presence (like a
non-empty `group_by` or `aggregates`) switches the query into grouped mode.

having.description:
HAVING: conditions on the aggregated groups, implicitly AND-ed. Only
meaningful in aggregated mode; a `var` term resolves to an aggregate value
or a GROUP BY key entity.

limit.description: Return at most this many rows (applied after `offset`).

max_solutions.description:
Fail-closed ceiling on the intermediate join solution set
(see `AnalyticQueryRequest::max_solutions`).

oneOf.description:
A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `eventual`, a floor not yet covered by the
published generation returns a retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429 (poll
until it lands); under `strong` the floor is satisfied by construction and a
floor above head is a client error. `None` == no floor. See
`docs/architecture/segment-native-indexing.md` §6.

order_by.description:
ORDER BY: sort keys applied to the result rows (or groups), in priority
order, before LIMIT/OFFSET.

patterns.description: WHERE: the conjunctive basic graph pattern (shares the analytic engine).

profile.description:
Return what the server measured while it answered this request in
`profile`. A profiled request never reads or fills the result cache,
so the profile always describes an execution.

reason.description:
Not available on the published SPARQL surface: a graph's stored
inference rules already run at publish time, folding derived facts into
the asserted dataset every query reads. Requesting `reason: true`
returns a typed, non-retryable error.

select.description:
SELECT projection: the variables to return, in order. Absent = `SELECT *`
(every variable the pattern binds, sorted). Ignored in aggregated mode.

SparqlSelectResponse.description:
Result of a `SparqlSelectRequest`. For SELECT, `vars` is the projected head
and `solutions` the rows; for ASK, `boolean` is set and `solutions` empty.

boolean.description: Set for the ASK form: whether the WHERE pattern has any solution.

groups.description: Aggregated/grouped result rows. Empty unless the query aggregates.

oneOf.description:
What the server measured for this request. Present only when the
request asked for `profile`.

solutions.description: Non-aggregated SELECT rows. Empty in aggregated mode and for ASK.

truncated.description:
The intermediate-solution ceiling cut the join
(see `AnalyticQueryResponse::truncated`).

vars.description:
The projected variable names (the result head). For aggregated queries
this is the GROUP BY keys followed by each aggregate's `as` variable.
Empty for ASK.

SparqlTerm.description: An operand in a FILTER comparison.

oneOf.description: The entity bound to a query variable.

var.description: The entity bound to a query variable.

oneOf.description: A literal property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.

property.description: A literal property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.

oneOf.description: A literal constant.

SparqlTextRequest.description:
Run a SPARQL 1.1 query supplied as **text** (SELECT or ASK) through the
conformant engine over the live graph, returning SPARQL 1.1 Query Results
JSON. Distinct from [`SparqlSelectRequest`] (the structured-request form);
this is the raw-text dialect. CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE are rejected (they yield an
RDF graph, not a results table).

oneOf.description:
Exact transaction-time watermark to read from a retained immutable
published generation. The server never reconstructs WAL state in the
request path and never substitutes a newer or older generation.

cursor.description:
Opt into snapshot-bound keyset pagination: empty string starts a page,
otherwise echo `next_cursor` with the identical query. Requires one
supported indexed ordered LIMIT (1..10000), OFFSET 0, and no transport
`limit`/`offset`. An unavailable snapshot expires the cursor explicitly.

entailment.description:
Entailment regime. `None` (default) matches asserted triples only.
`Rdfs` applies the practical RDFS core at query time, `Subclass` the
class-only subset, and `Owl` the OWL profile on top of `Rdfs`. All
derive the closure from the pinned generation's asserted schema
triples.

limit.description:
Return at most this many result rows. Applied to SELECT bindings after the
conformant engine has produced the complete result document.

offset.description: Skip this many result rows before `limit`.

profile.description:
Return what the server measured while it answered this request in
`profile`. A profiled request never reads or fills the result cache,
so the profile always describes an execution.

query.description: The SPARQL query text (SELECT or ASK).

reason.description:
Not available on the published SPARQL surface: a graph's stored
inference rules already run at publish time, folding derived facts into
the asserted dataset every query reads. Requesting `reason: true`
returns a typed, non-retryable error.

request.description:
The user's words behind this query, when the caller has them. When
present the server records an eval trace and returns its `trace_id`,
so the caller can label the result valid or not (managed evals).

SparqlTextResponse.description:
Result of a [`SparqlTextRequest`]: the SPARQL 1.1 Query Results JSON document,
carried verbatim as a string (the engine already serializes it to the
standard `{ "head": …, "results": … }` / `{ "head": …, "boolean": … }`
shape). Clients parse `results` as JSON.

next_cursor.description:
Continuation for the query's inner ordered window. OPTIONAL enrichment
can return more rows than that window. Absent when exhausted or when
cursor pagination was not requested; a full final page may yield a
continuation whose following page is empty.

oneOf.description:
